content.text:
ztd-query-phpでphp-ai-toolkitを適用し、その上で最適化しました。
これはmonorepo独自の部分もありますが基本骨子としてはこれが最上です。

ztd-query-phpの設定内容を確認し、これをフィードバックとしてphp-ai-toolkitに適用してください。
とりあえずわかったこととして
・fuzzはentrypointとtargetのみを置くぐらいシンプルに作り込むのがいい
　・契約を満たすか性質を満たすかで内容が変わる
　・契約を満たすならFuzzerのBytesを元に入力して異常動作しないことを確認
　・性質を満たすならFuzzerのBytesを元に入力して、期待した結果、振る舞いになるかを確認
・fuzzはメインリポジトリのみで実行
　・FuzzのCIは常にグリーンでレッドになるのはFuzzerが進行できない重大なバグが起きた時のみ（DBが落ちたとか）
　・crashはCIではグリーンとして扱い、Issueに報告すること
・Mutationは重いのでメインリポジトリのみで実行
　・Mutationの扱いもFuzzと同じでIssueを立てるために使う

この辺はよくAIと認識ズレが起きるなという印象です。これだけではありませんがこの話も含めてztd-query-phpのリモートのmainの最新状態を分析して取り込んでください。
まず ztd-query-php のリモート main の最新状態を取得し、php-ai-toolkit の skills/docs と突き合わせて差分を分析します。

result.output:
name: Fuzz (sql-parser)

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '47 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      max_runs:
        description: Maximum mutation iterations after the initial corpus is replayed
        required: true
        default: '10000'
        type: string
      mysql_version:
        description: MySQL release whose grammar the MySQL target parses with
        required: true
        default: '8.4.7'
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
  MYSQL_VERSION: ${{ inputs.mysql_version || '8.4.7' }}

jobs:
  parse:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    name: Parse / ${{ matrix.target.database }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target:
          - { database: mysql, script: fuzz_mysql_parse.php, extensions: 'mbstring, pcntl, zlib' }
          - { database: pg, script: fuzz_pg_parse.php, extensions: 'mbstring, pcntl, zlib' }
          - { database: sqlite, script: fuzz_sqlite_parse.php, extensions: 'mbstring, pcntl, zlib' }
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/sql-parser
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: ${{ matrix.target.extensions }}
          coverage: none
      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-parser
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: true
      - name: Check runtime platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs --no-dev
      - name: Validate the manual run budget
        env:
          FUZZ_MAX_RUNS: ${{ inputs.max_runs || '10000' }}
        run: |
          case "$FUZZ_MAX_RUNS" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 'max_runs must be a positive integer.' >&2; exit 2 ;;
          esac
          if [ "${#FUZZ_MAX_RUNS}" -gt 8 ] || [ "$FUZZ_MAX_RUNS" -lt 1 ]; then
            echo 'max_runs must be between 1 and 99999999.' >&2
            exit 2
          fi
      - name: Restore the evolving raw-input corpus
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: packages/sql-parser/fuzz/corpus/${{ matrix.target.database }}
          key: sql-parser-corpus-v1-${{ matrix.target.database }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          restore-keys: sql-parser-corpus-v1-${{ matrix.target.database }}-
      - name: Restore grammar coverage snapshots independently of the corpus
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: packages/sql-parser/fuzz/coverage/${{ matrix.target.database }}
          key: sql-parser-coverage-v1-${{ matrix.target.database }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          restore-keys: sql-parser-coverage-v1-${{ matrix.target.database }}-
      - name: Run PHP-Fuzzer
        env:
          FUZZ_MAX_RUNS: ${{ inputs.max_runs || '10000' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p build/fuzz "fuzz/corpus/${{ matrix.target.database }}"
          vendor/bin/php-fuzzer fuzz \
            "fuzz/${{ matrix.target.script }}" \
            "fuzz/corpus/${{ matrix.target.database }}/" \
            "--max-runs=$FUZZ_MAX_RUNS" 2>&1 | tee "build/fuzz/${{ matrix.target.database }}.log"
      - name: Open an issue for a finding
        uses: actions/github-script@ed597411d8f924073f98dfc5c65a23a2325f34cd
        env:
          FUZZ_DATABASE: ${{ matrix.target.database }}
          FUZZ_SCRIPT: ${{ matrix.target.script }}
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('node:fs');
            const path = require('node:path');
            const crypto = require('node:crypto');
            const database = process.env.FUZZ_DATABASE;
            const script = process.env.FUZZ_SCRIPT;
            const root = path.resolve('packages/sql-parser');
            const log = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, `build/fuzz/${database}.log`), 'utf8');
            const finding = log.match(/^(?:CORPUS )?CRASH in (.+)!$/m);
            if (!finding) return;
            const input = fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(root, finding[1]));
            const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(input).digest('hex');
            const marker = `<!-- sql-parser-fuzz:${database}:${hash} -->`;
            const issues = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listForRepo, {
              ...context.repo, state: 'open', per_page: 100
            });
            if (issues.some(issue => !issue.pull_request && issue.body?.includes(marker))) return;
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = [
              marker,
              `PHP-Fuzzer found a statement the ${database} parser rejects.`,
              `Commit: ${context.sha}`,
              `Workflow and input artifact: ${run} (sql-parser-fuzz-${database})`,
              'Run from packages/sql-parser after extracting the artifact:',
              '```sh',
              `vendor/bin/php-fuzzer run-single fuzz/${script} '${finding[1]}'`,
              '```',
              `Input SHA-256: ${hash}`,
              '<details><summary>PHP-Fuzzer output</summary>',
              '', '```text', log.slice(-45000), '```', '</details>'
            ].join('\n\n');
            await github.rest.issues.create({
              ...context.repo,
              title: `[sql-parser fuzz] ${database}: ${hash.slice(0, 12)}`,
              body
            });
      - name: Save the evolving corpus
        if: always()
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: packages/sql-parser/fuzz/corpus/${{ matrix.target.database }}
          key: sql-parser-corpus-v1-${{ matrix.target.database }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      - name: Save grammar coverage history
        if: always()
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: packages/sql-parser/fuzz/coverage/${{ matrix.target.database }}
          key: sql-parser-coverage-v1-${{ matrix.target.database }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      - name: Upload PHP-Fuzzer inputs, output and grammar coverage
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: sql-parser-fuzz-${{ matrix.target.database }}
          path: |
            packages/sql-parser/crash-*
            packages/sql-parser/build/fuzz/${{ matrix.target.database }}.log
            packages/sql-parser/fuzz/corpus/${{ matrix.target.database }}/
            packages/sql-parser/fuzz/coverage/${{ matrix.target.database }}/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

name: Mutation (sql-parser)

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '28 2 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: mutation-sql-parser

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
    working-directory: packages/sql-parser

jobs:
  mutation:
    name: Mutation Testing
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: ctype, date, dom, filter, hash, iconv, json, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, pcre, pdo, phar, reflection, simplexml, spl, tokenizer, xml, xmlwriter, zlib
          coverage: pcov
          tools: infection:0.35.4
          ini-values: memory_limit=1G
      - name: Validate the Composer manifest and lock file
        run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
      - name: Install package dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          working-directory: packages/sql-parser
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: true
      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: |
          composer check-platform-reqs --no-dev
          infection --version
      - name: Mutation testing on the whole source tree
        run: >-
          php -d memory_limit=4G "$(command -v infection)"
          --configuration=infection.json5 --with-uncovered
          --threads=4
          --only-covering-test-cases
          --min-msi=0 --min-covered-msi=0 --no-progress
          --logger-github
      - name: Reject skipped whole-tree mutants
        run: |
          php -d memory_limit=4G -r '
            $report = json_decode(file_get_contents("build/infection/infection.json"), true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
            if (($report["stats"]["skippedCount"] ?? null) !== 0) {
                fwrite(STDERR, "Infection skipped mutants before execution; review the timeout against test durations.\n");
                exit(1);
            }
          '
      - name: Create or update the package MSI issue
        if: success()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/github-script@ed597411d8f924073f98dfc5c65a23a2325f34cd
        env:
          # Keep these alert thresholds aligned with this package's infection.json5.
          MIN_MSI: '80'
          MIN_COVERED_MSI: '80'
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('node:fs');
            const stats = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('packages/sql-parser/build/infection/infection.json', 'utf8')).stats;
            const minMsi = Number(process.env.MIN_MSI);
            const minCoveredMsi = Number(process.env.MIN_COVERED_MSI);
            for (const value of [stats.msi, stats.coveredCodeMsi, minMsi, minCoveredMsi]) {
              if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0 || value > 100) {
                throw new Error('Infection must report valid MSI percentages and thresholds.');
              }
            }
            const belowThreshold = stats.msi < minMsi || stats.coveredCodeMsi < minCoveredMsi;
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const marker = '<!-- mutation-msi:sql-parser -->';
            const title = '[sql-parser] Mutation testing MSI below threshold';
            const body = [
              marker,
              'Daily mutation testing on `main` is below the required score for `sql-parser`.',
              '',
              '| Metric | Actual | Required |',
              '| --- | ---: | ---: |',
              `| MSI | ${stats.msi}% | ${minMsi}% |`,
              `| Covered MSI | ${stats.coveredCodeMsi}% | ${minCoveredMsi}% |`,
              '',
              `Commit: ${context.sha}`,
              `Run and mutation reports: ${run}`,
              `Run attempt: ${process.env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}`,
              '',
              'MSI thresholds are reported here without failing the workflow.'
            ].join('\n');
            await core.summary
              .addHeading('Mutation testing: sql-parser')
              .addRaw(`MSI: ${stats.msi}% (required: ${minMsi}%). Covered MSI: ${stats.coveredCodeMsi}% (required: ${minCoveredMsi}%).`)
              .write();
            if (!belowThreshold) return;
            const issues = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listForRepo, {
              ...context.repo, state: 'all', per_page: 100
            });
            const existing = issues.find(issue => !issue.pull_request && (
              issue.body?.includes(marker) || issue.title === title
            ));
            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.update({ ...context.repo, issue_number: existing.number, body });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.create({ ...context.repo, title, body });
            }
      - name: Upload mutation reports
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: sql-parser-infection
          path: packages/sql-parser/build/infection/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

input.description: Show sql-parser fuzz entrypoint

result.output:
<?php

/**
 * PHP-Fuzzer entry point: every MySQL statement sql-faker generates must parse.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   MYSQL_VERSION=8.4.7 vendor/bin/php-fuzzer fuzz fuzz/fuzz_mysql_parse.php fuzz/corpus/mysql/
 *
 * Environment variables:
 *   MYSQL_VERSION     - MySQL release to test (default: 8.4.7)
 *                       Supported: 5.6.51, 5.7.44, 8.0.44, 8.1.0, 8.2.0, 8.3.0, 8.4.7, 9.0.1, 9.1.0
 *   SQLFAKER_COVERAGE - Set to 0 to run without recording grammar coverage under fuzz/coverage/mysql
 */

declare(strict_types=1);

use Faker\Factory;
use Fuzz\Target\ParseTarget;
use SqlFaker\Generation\Choice\BytePlanCompiler;
use SqlFaker\Generation\Coverage\GrammarCoverage;
use SqlFaker\Generation\Plan\GenerationPlan;
use SqlFaker\MySql\MySqlProvider;
use SqlParser\MySql\MySqlParser;

$mysqlVersion = getenv('MYSQL_VERSION') !== false ? getenv('MYSQL_VERSION') : '8.4.7';

/**
 * Grammar version and the statement rule to generate from. Statements start below the
 * grammar entry point, which also lists parser-internal selectors the lexer never produces.
 */
$roots = [
    '5.6.51' => 'statement',
    '5.7.44' => 'statement',
    '8.0.44' => 'simple_statement_or_begin',
    '8.1.0' => 'simple_statement_or_begin',
    '8.2.0' => 'simple_statement_or_begin',
    '8.3.0' => 'simple_statement_or_begin',
    '8.4.7' => 'simple_statement_or_begin',
    '9.0.1' => 'simple_statement_or_begin',
    '9.1.0' => 'simple_statement_or_begin',
];

if (!isset($roots[$mysqlVersion])) {
    fwrite(STDERR, "Unknown MySQL version: {$mysqlVersion}\n");
    fwrite(STDERR, 'Supported versions: ' . implode(', ', array_keys($roots)) . "\n");
    exit(1);
}

$grammarVersion = "mysql-{$mysqlVersion}";
$coverage = getenv('SQLFAKER_COVERAGE') === '0' ? null : new GrammarCoverage(__DIR__ . '/coverage/mysql');
$provider = new MySqlProvider(Factory::create(), $grammarVersion, $coverage);
$parser = new MySqlParser($grammarVersion);
$target = new ParseTarget(static fn (string $sql): SqlParser\Parser\Node => $parser->parse($sql), $grammarVersion);
$planner = $provider->planner();
$constraints = GenerationPlan::fromRule($roots[$mysqlVersion])->requiringNonEmpty();

/**
 * The plan compiler reads four budget bytes and then one decision per byte, so inputs
 * are allowed to grow well beyond php-fuzzer's default length.
 *
 * @var PhpFuzzer\Config $config
 */
$config->setAllowedExceptions([]);
$config->setMaxLen(80004);
$config->setTarget(static function (string $input) use ($provider, $planner, $constraints, $target): void {
    $plan = (new BytePlanCompiler())->compile($input, $planner, $constraints);
    $target->verify($provider->generate($plan), $input);
});

input.description: Show sql-parser fuzz target

result.output:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Fuzz\Target;

use Closure;
use Error;
use SqlParser\Lexer\SourceException;
use SqlParser\Parser\Node;

/**
 * Parses generated SQL and reports a statement the grammar should have accepted.
 *
 * Every statement sql-faker generates is derived from the same grammar the
 * parse table was built from, so a rejection is a finding: it surfaces as
 * an Error for PHP-Fuzzer to record together with the input. So is a tree
 * that does not write back the statement it was parsed from, byte for byte,
 * because the tree is meant to hold every byte of the text, comments and
 * whitespace included.
 */
final class ParseTarget
{
    /**
     * @param Closure(string): Node $parse Parses one statement, throwing on rejection
     * @param string $grammarVersion Grammar version that produced the statement, e.g. "mysql-8.4.7"
     */
    public function __construct(
        private readonly Closure $parse,
        private readonly string $grammarVersion,
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * Verifies that the parser accepts the generated statement and writes it back unchanged.
     *
     * @param string $sql Statement produced by the grammar
     * @param string $input Fuzzer input that produced the statement, so a finding can be replayed
     *
     * @throws Error When the statement is empty, the parser rejects it, or the tree writes back other text
     */
    public function verify(string $sql, string $input): void
    {
        if ($sql === '') {
            throw new Error("Statement generation returned an empty string\nInput (hex): " . bin2hex($input));
        }
        try {
            $tree = ($this->parse)($sql);
        } catch (SourceException $rejection) {
            throw new Error(
                "The parser rejected generated SQL\n" .
                "Grammar: {$this->grammarVersion}\n" .
                'Input (hex): ' . bin2hex($input) . "\n" .
                "SQL: {$sql}\n" .
                "Error: {$rejection->getMessage()}",
                0,
                $rejection,
            );
        }
        $printed = $tree->toString();
        if ($printed !== $sql) {
            throw new Error(
                "The tree wrote back other text than the generated SQL\n" .
                "Grammar: {$this->grammarVersion}\n" .
                'Input (hex): ' . bin2hex($input) . "\n" .
                'Diverges at byte: ' . strspn($sql ^ $printed, "\0") . "\n" .
                "SQL: {$sql}\n" .
                "Tree: {$printed}",
            );
        }
    }
}

2	# AGENTS
3	
4	## This Project
5	
6	This project builds a complete Zero Table Dependency (ZTD) implementation for PHP.
7	
8	ZTD runs tests on a real database engine without ever touching a physical table. Before a query reaches the database, every table it references is replaced by a CTE holding fixture rows (CTE shadowing), and every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE is turned into a SELECT that returns the rows the write would produce (result select query). Those rows are kept in the session, so later queries see the writes. One empty schema serves every test: no migrations, no seeding, no cleanup, and tests run in parallel without interfering.
9	
10	The hard part is "complete". A rewrite must keep the meaning of whatever SQL the application sends, in every dialect and version, and a rewrite that is slightly wrong does not fail: it silently returns wrong test results. Hand-picked test cases cannot establish that. ZTD has to understand SQL exactly as the server does, and its behavior has to be checked against the server itself.
11	
12	That is why the repository holds so many packages. The `ztd-query-*` packages are the product, split only so that users install the dialect and driver they need. Everything else exists for quality, and it is the core of this project: reading the official grammars instead of approximating them, parsing and binding SQL the way the server does, generating every statement form the grammars allow, running the statements against the real servers and comparing the results, and tracing each specification back to the manual it comes from. Correctness comes from that machinery, not from examples.
13	
14	The repository is also an experiment in how AI agents can build something this complex correctly, so every claim about behavior has to be backed by tests, fuzzing, or a specification.

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-fuzzing
3	description: >-
4	  Set up contract-driven fuzzing for a PHP project, including domain-aware input
5	  generation, meaningful oracles, reproducible corpora and crashes, Composer
6	  commands, and a separate scheduled GitHub Actions workflow. Use for parsers,
7	  protocols, SQL, HTTP endpoints, file formats, adapters, or other surfaces where
8	  coverage-guided input exploration is useful. Use setup-toolkit-pbt instead when
9	  structured values and shrinkable properties are the better fit.
10	---
11	
12	# Set Up Contract-Driven Fuzzing
13	
14	Fuzzing is useful only after the contract under test is explicit. Do not add a
15	loop that feeds arbitrary strings to an arbitrary method and calls a lack of
16	crashes success.
17	
18	The design in `k-kinzal/ztd-query-php` is the reference shape: SQL Faker compiles
19	fuzzer bytes into generation plans and prepares the resulting SQL on native
20	databases; adapter correctness targets compare native and wrapped behavior. Its
21	exact SQL generators, database versions, dependencies, run counts, and workflow topology
22	are examples, not defaults for another project.
23	
24	## Inspect the Target Project
25	
26	Read before choosing a tool or editing files:
27	
28	- `composer.json`, every maintained lock file, PHP constraints, autoload roots,
29	  test scripts, and development dependencies;
30	- public API and protocol documentation for the requested surface;
31	- existing unit, integration, property, fixture, parser, schema, and end-to-end
32	  tests that reveal accepted and rejected inputs;
33	- existing fuzz targets, corpora, crash files, dictionaries, generators, service
34	  containers, and `.gitignore` rules; and
35	- all GitHub Actions workflows, including their PHP runtime, extensions, service
36	  versions, lock policy, action pins, permissions, and timeouts.
37	
38	Preserve unrelated changes. Never point a fuzzer at production or at a shared
39	environment. Starting a local disposable service is in scope for setup; fuzzing an
40	external service requires the user's explicit authorization for that exact target.
41	
42	Keep campaign instructions with an existing development-owned `fuzz/` surface when
43	needed. Do not add fuzz setup, coverage reports, or reproduction tooling to the
44	product README or `docs/` unless that documentation is requested.
45	
46	## Define the Contract First
47	
48	For each target, identify all of the following before implementing it:
49	
50	| Question | Required decision |
51	|----------|-------------------|
52	| Surface | The exact parser, public method, HTTP route, adapter, query pipeline, file reader, or state transition exercised |
53	| Input domain | Which values are valid, invalid-but-expected, and outside scope; include dialect, protocol, schema, and version |
54	| Property | What must remain true for every generated case |
55	| Oracle | How a violation is distinguished from an allowed rejection |
56	| State | What must be reset before every input and what state transitions are intentionally explored |
57	| Environment | Runtime, extensions, database/server versions, fixtures, authentication, and resource limits |
58	| Reproduction | Which bytes, seed, generated request, environment versions, and command are needed to rerun a failure |
59	
60	Prefer a narrow target with a strong oracle over a broad target whose only check is
61	"did not crash." Create separate targets when surfaces have different contracts,
62	generators, state, or oracles. Name Composer scripts and CI matrix entries after
63	the contract, such as `fuzz:parser:json`, `fuzz:http:orders`, or
64	`fuzz:sql:select-correctness`.
65	
66	### Choose Fuzzing or PBT Deliberately
67	
68	Use coverage-guided fuzzing when mutated byte sequences or corpus evolution can
69	discover new control flow: parsers, decoders, query languages, wire protocols,
70	file formats, request routing, escaping, and deep state machines are common fits.
71	
72	Use `/setup-toolkit-pbt` when inputs are naturally structured PHP values, the
73	important statement is an algebraic, model, round-trip, or state-transition
74	property, and automatic shrinking will produce a better counterexample. Both may
75	be appropriate for one component, but they must assert different contracts rather
76	than duplicate an expensive random loop in two runners.
77	
78	## Select the Input Mechanism and Oracle Together
79	
80	Choose the generator from the language the target actually accepts:
81	
82	| Contract surface | Input mechanism | Strong oracle examples |
83	|------------------|-----------------|------------------------|
84	| Raw bytes or a tolerant parser | Coverage-guided byte mutation, a small valid/invalid corpus, and a token dictionary | No engine-level error, bounded resource use, parse/print/parse equivalence |
85	| SQL or another grammar | Versioned grammar- or AST-based generation; make fuzzer input select productions, complexity, and seed | Native parser/database acceptance, differential results, rewrite equivalence, query-plan invariants |
86	| OpenAPI HTTP service | An OpenAPI-aware generator when the specification is authoritative; custom schema/state generators otherwise | Status/schema contract, reference model, idempotency, authorization and resource-lifecycle invariants |
87	| Serializer or codec | Structured value generator plus valid and corrupted encoded corpus | Decode(encode(x)), canonicalization, alternate implementation comparison |
88	| Database or protocol adapter | Schema-aware operations and disposable real services at supported versions | Native client versus adapter results, errors, transactions, and resulting state |
89	| Stateful domain workflow | Command generator constrained by the current model state | Model state versus system state after every command; reset per sequence |
90	
91	For HTTP, generate method, path, headers, authentication state, content type, and
92	body coherently. Randomizing only the body does not test the HTTP contract. Cover
93	both specification-valid requests and intentionally invalid classes, and assert
94	their different expected outcomes. Do not treat every 4xx or 5xx response as
95	equivalent; classify allowed rejection codes and fail on contract-breaking or
96	server-error responses.
97	
98	For SQL, start from the supported dialect and version rather than concatenating
99	keywords. Reuse an appropriate grammar generator such as SQL Faker when it covers
100	the target dialect, or build a schema-aware AST generator when semantic validity
101	matters. Validate grammar-generated SQL against the real database parser before
102	claiming syntax correctness. For adapters and rewriters, run the same schema,
103	fixtures, query, and transaction through the native and wrapped paths and compare
104	normalized results and final state.
105	
106	A syntax target should reach the server's parser/prepare operation without
107	executing arbitrary generated statements. Verify the driver does not emulate or
108	rewrite the input before the server sees it. Use execution and fixture state only
109	for contracts that actually require them, such as adapter correctness.
110	
111	### Make Fuzzer Bytes Useful
112	
113	The target must be deterministic for the same input and environment. Raw fuzzer
114	bytes may be consumed directly, used to select generator branches and complexity,
115	or converted to a reproducible seed. Prefer consuming bytes across structural
116	choices because nearby mutations can then produce nearby cases. When the product
117	has a plan/compiler API, use it to freeze production choices, values, and budgets;
118	later random state must not change replay. A whole-input hash or CRC seed is only
119	a fallback for a generator without structural controls. Verify useful corpus and
120	coverage growth before treating that bridge as sufficient.
121	
122	Bound recursion, collection sizes, request sequences, payload length, and per-input
123	work. Keep boundary values, empty values, malformed encodings, duplicate fields,
124	ordering changes, and version-specific constructs reachable. Do not make only
125	happy-path inputs reachable.
126	
127	## Build a Real Oracle
128	
129	Use one or more of these oracle forms:
130	
131	- differential: compare with a native implementation, previous compatible
132	  version, alternate parser, or reference service;
133	- round-trip: parse/render/parse or encode/decode while accounting for documented
134	  normalization;
135	- metamorphic: apply a transformation that should preserve or predictably change
136	  behavior;
137	- model-based: compare every operation and state transition with a small reference
138	  model;
139	- invariant: determinism, idempotence, classification/rewrite agreement, row-count
140	  rules, authorization boundaries, transaction behavior, or bounded resources.
141	
142	"No crash" is sufficient only for a deliberately named robustness target. It is
143	not a correctness oracle.
144	
145	Classify expected rejections by stable exception type, error code, response class,
146	or documented predicate. Do not catch `Throwable`, all database errors, or all 4xx
147	responses and return. In PHP-Fuzzer, ordinary exceptions are ignored while
148	`Error` represents a finding, so convert unexpected exceptions and explicit
149	contract mismatches to an `Error` that prints the target name, fuzzer input or
150	seed, generated domain input, and relevant environment versions. Keep the allowed
151	rejection list narrow and explain each entry.
152	
153	Keep allowed rejections in a readable target-owned table with the reason beside
154	each code. When one code represents both syntax and semantic failures, use a
155	source-verified predicate for the allowed case. A dead connection, missing service,
156	or broken instrumentation is a campaign failure and must stop with a non-zero
157	status, not disappear as an ordinary ignored exception or become a product crash.
158	
159	Reset mutable state in `finally` after every input. For stateful sequences, reset
160	between sequences, not between operations within the sequence. A crash must not be
161	caused by state leaked from an unrelated previous input.
162	
163	## Keep the Harness Small
164	
165	Let the fuzz engine own the campaign loop, input mutation, corpus evolution, crash
166	files, and minimization. The target should compose environment setup, input-to-plan
167	conversion, one product operation, and its oracle. Do not build a second campaign
168	runner, verdict registry, witness database, acceptance dashboard, or native
169	extension merely to apply this skill.
170	
171	Keep reusable planning and domain coverage in the product that owns those
172	concepts. The fuzz target can enable its recorder; it should not build a parallel
173	coverage model or feed every oracle verdict back into production. Add custom
174	engine feedback only for demonstrated coverage gaps the normal engine cannot see.
175	
176	Verify a thin harness through bounded execution and crash replay rather than
177	creating a unit/integration suite for its wiring. Test substantive product
178	algorithms and nontrivial oracle decisions where needed, using visible fixtures
179	and the test framework's assertions instead of a bespoke testing framework.
180	
181	## PHP-Fuzzer Setup
182	
183	PHP-Fuzzer is the normal starting point for coverage-guided PHP targets, not an
184	universal requirement. Inspect its current release, PHP and `nikic/php-parser`
185	constraints, target API, CLI, and required extensions at application time. Test
186	resolution against every lock/runtime that will install development dependencies:
187	
188	```bash
189	composer require --dev "nikic/php-fuzzer:<target-derived-constraint>" --dry-run
190	composer why-not nikic/php-fuzzer <newest-compatible-version>
191	```
192	
193	Run the confirmed requirement without `--dry-run`. Do not copy the version from
194	this toolkit or from `ztd-query-php`. Do not widen the project's parser constraint
195	or drop supported PHP versions merely to install the fuzzer. When the dependency
196	graph conflicts, choose a compatible engine or a genuinely isolated fuzz-tool
197	environment that still loads the target against its real dependencies.
198	
199	A PHP-Fuzzer entry point must register a `callable(string): void` with
200	`$config->setTarget()`. Use `setMaxLen()` when larger inputs add cost without adding
201	useful cases, and add a dictionary for syntax handled outside instrumented PHP
202	code. Keep setup outside the per-input callable; keep mutable target state inside
203	the reset boundary.
204	
205	## Project Layout and Commands
206	
207	Use a dedicated top-level `fuzz/` tree unless the project has an established
208	equivalent:
209	
210	```text
211	fuzz/
212	|-- <target>.php
213	|-- <Contract>/...          target-specific generators, models, and comparators
214	`-- corpus/<target>/...     a small reviewed seed corpus plus generated entries
215	```
216	
217	Add target support classes to `autoload-dev` with a project-derived namespace and
218	run `composer dump-autoload`. Keep reviewed seeds when they unlock meaningful
219	states or reproduce a defect. Do not manufacture fixed binary seeds or add a
220	corpus-preparation program just to populate a directory: an engine-generated
221	corpus is sufficient when the byte-to-plan mapping already reaches useful cases.
222	Let local and CI runs evolve it. Ignore generated corpus entries and root `crash-*`
223	files without untracking reviewed seeds; force-add a deliberately promoted seed
224	when needed.
225	Never commit credentials, production data, access tokens, or sensitive HTTP
226	responses in a corpus or crash artifact.
227	
228	Add one Composer script per contract and an aggregate only when running all targets
229	locally is useful:
230	
231	```json
232	{
233	    "scripts": {
234	        "fuzz": [
235	            "@fuzz:REPLACE_WITH_CONTRACT"
236	        ],
237	        "fuzz:REPLACE_WITH_CONTRACT": "php-fuzzer fuzz fuzz/REPLACE_WITH_TARGET.php fuzz/corpus/REPLACE_WITH_CONTRACT/"
238	    }
239	}
240	```
241	
242	Keep fuzzing out of `test`, `test:unit`, `lint`, and ParaTest scripts. A bounded
243	local smoke command may be added as `fuzz:smoke`, but it is not a substitute for
244	the scheduled campaign.
245	
246	## GitHub Actions
247	
248	Read `fuzz.yml` from
249	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-fuzzing/` and apply it as a
250	separate `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`. Do not merge an unbounded or scheduled fuzz
251	campaign into ordinary pull-request tests.
252	
253	PHP-Fuzzer separates findings from campaign failures at the process level:
254	`php-fuzzer fuzz` records a finding as a `crash-*` file and still exits zero,
255	while a non-zero exit means the campaign itself was impeded — a usage error, a
256	`FuzzerException`, broken instrumentation, or a dead process. Keep that
257	separation in the workflow: findings surface as crash artifacts on a green run,
258	and as issue creation only when the user has asked for it, while a red run means
259	the campaign could not execute. Do not wrap the fuzzer in exit-code handling
260	that turns a finding into a step failure or a step failure into success.
261	
262	Replace every `REPLACE_WITH_*` sentinel from the target project. Expand the target
263	matrix so each entry has one contract, corpus, and required extension set. Add
264	service/container setup before the fuzzer when the oracle needs a real database or
265	HTTP service, and put supported server versions in the matrix only when the
266	contract differs by version.
267	
268	The workflow must:
269	
270	- run on a deliberate schedule and `workflow_dispatch`, normally on one selected
271	  fuzz-tool PHP runtime rather than the compatibility matrix;
272	- validate the manual run budget before passing it to a shell command;
273	- restore and save each target's corpus with separate keys;
274	- upload crash files whether the fuzzer step succeeds or fails: findings arrive
275	  on a green step, and an impeded campaign may still have written crashes before
276	  stopping;
277	- use job timeouts as a second bound in addition to `--max-runs` or the selected
278	  engine's time limit;
279	- pin external actions to full commit SHAs, use `contents: read`, and avoid write
280	  permissions unless the user explicitly asks for issue creation or another
281	  mutation; and
282	- use disposable local services and non-secret synthetic fixtures.
283	
284	Scheduled workflows run from the default branch, so the schedule becomes active
285	only after that workflow exists there. Choose a minute away from the start of the
286	hour to reduce scheduler congestion. Keep `workflow_dispatch` so a crash fix, new
287	corpus, or changed generator can be exercised immediately.
288	
289	## Failure Triage and Regression
290	
291	Reproduce a PHP-Fuzzer finding with the same environment, then minimize it:
292	
293	```bash
294	vendor/bin/php-fuzzer run-single fuzz/REPLACE_WITH_TARGET.php crash-REPLACE_WITH_HASH
295	vendor/bin/php-fuzzer minimize-crash fuzz/REPLACE_WITH_TARGET.php crash-REPLACE_WITH_HASH
296	```
297	
298	Confirm the minimized input fails repeatedly. Determine whether it is a product
299	bug, generator bug, invalid oracle, resource-limit breach, or intentionally allowed
300	rejection. Fix the cause; do not broaden a catch block or allowed-error list merely
301	to make the finding disappear. Promote the minimized case to a deterministic
302	regression test or reviewed seed corpus, then keep the fuzz target so related cases
303	remain discoverable.
304	
305	## Verification
306	
307	Before completing setup:
308	
309	1. Run each entry point once with a tiny bounded budget and confirm it executes the
310	   intended production code.
311	2. Give the target a disposable known-bad oracle or input and confirm the run
312	   reports the crash and writes a reproducible `crash-*` file; with PHP-Fuzzer
313	   the process still exits zero. Remove the probe afterward.
314	3. Run `run-single` on that crash and verify the diagnostic contains the contract,
315	   domain input or seed, and environment version.
316	4. Confirm state is reset by running the same corpus twice in one process.
317	5. Check that any reviewed seeds are tracked, generated corpus and crashes are ignored,
318	   and no sensitive data is present.
319	6. Run `composer validate --strict --no-check-publish`, the normal unit suite, and
320	   every bounded fuzz Composer command.
321	7. Run `git diff --check` and validate `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml` with actionlint.
322	8. Search for remaining sentinels; any `REPLACE_WITH` in installed project files is
323	   a failed setup.
324	
325	## References
326	
327	- [ztd-query-php fuzz targets and workflows](https://github.com/k-kinzal/ztd-query-php) — Grammar-aware SQL generation, invariants, differential database oracles, corpus caching, and crash artifacts.
328	- [PHP-Fuzzer](https://github.com/nikic/PHP-Fuzzer) — Target API, corpus, dictionary, crash minimization, and coverage reports.
329	- [GitHub Actions workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax) — Schedules, manual inputs, permissions, concurrency, and job timeouts.
330	- [GitHub Actions security hardening](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) — Action pinning and least privilege.

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-infection
3	description: >-
4	  Set up Infection mutation testing for a PHP project. Use when asked to configure
5	  Infection, infection.json5, mutation testing, mutation score (MSI) or covered MSI
6	  thresholds, a mutation score gate that differs between the default branch and pull
7	  requests, mutation testing of changed lines only, Composer scripts for Infection,
8	  CI jobs for mutation testing, or when asked why a test suite with high coverage
9	  still lets mutants escape.
10	---
11	
12	# Setup Infection (Mutation Testing)
13	
14	This skill configures Infection, the PHP mutation testing framework, as a quality
15	gate with two thresholds: one for the whole source tree and a stricter one for the
16	lines a pull request changes.
17	
18	Line coverage says a line ran. Mutation testing says the tests noticed what the line
19	did. It is the check that catches the failure mode this toolkit exists for:
20	AI-generated tests that execute code and assert nothing meaningful about it.
21	
22	## Prerequisites
23	
24	Inspect the project before configuring:
25	
26	- Confirm the project requires `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit` and has a working PHPUnit
27	  setup (`/setup-toolkit-phpunit`).
28	- Read `composer.json`: production autoload roots, the PHP floor, existing test and
29	  coverage scripts, and `config.allow-plugins`.
30	- Check for existing mutation config: `infection.json`, `infection.json5`, or either
31	  with a `.dist` suffix.
32	- Check that a coverage driver is available. Infection needs pcov or Xdebug.
33	
34	Determine Infection's installation topology before choosing its version. Inspect
35	the target's PHP range, PHPUnit version, Composer locks, and the PHP runtime of the
36	mutation job. Then inspect current Composer metadata and Infection's release/schema
37	documentation and select the newest compatible release. Do not copy this toolkit
38	repository's historical multi-line constraint.
39	
40	If root development dependencies install on every supported PHP minor, derive the
41	smallest constraint that lets each real graph resolve its newest compatible
42	Infection release. Prefer one current line; add an older line only for a supported
43	leg that proves it is necessary. If the package graph forces an unsuitable tool
44	release, prefer a pinned Infection PHAR on the mutation job's supported runtime.
45	Do not create a nested `tools/infection/composer.json` and lock just to isolate one
46	executable. Preserve an established separate toolchain only when the project
47	deliberately maintains it. Verify every relevant lock or CI leg and diagnose an
48	unexpected resolution with `composer why-not`:
49	
50	```bash
51	composer require --dev "infection/infection:<target-derived-constraint>" --dry-run
52	composer why-not infection/infection <newest-compatible-version>
53	```
54	
55	Run the confirmed requirement without `--dry-run`, then enable the plugin only if
56	the resolved package requires it. Do not assume the minimum PHP version or supported
57	Infection line from this repository; those are release properties to verify at
58	application time.
59	
60	For a PHAR installation, `setup-php` can install `infection:<exact-version>` in
61	its `tools` input. Resolve that version from the mutation runtime, verify
62	`infection --version`, use the matching published `resources/schema.json` URL,
63	and replace `vendor/bin/infection` in every command with the installed executable.
64	When passing PHP options, invoke `php -d memory_limit=4G "$(command -v infection)"`.
65	The product still installs its own locked dependencies and PHPUnit; a PHAR does not
66	make an incompatible test graph supported. No Infection Composer plugin permission
67	is needed for this installation mode.
68	
69	## Templates
70	
71	Read the templates from
72	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-infection/` and apply them to
73	the project root:
74	
75	| Template | Target | Scope |
76	|----------|--------|-------|
77	| `infection.json5` | `infection.json5` | The only configuration file |
78	| `mutation-job.yml` | merge into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI job for both gates |
79	
80	Write one configuration file, not one per gate. Infection reads a single file and
81	takes per-run thresholds from `--min-msi` and `--min-covered-msi`, which is how its
82	own documentation drives CI. A second file duplicates the scope, the mutators, and
83	the exclusions, and the day one copy is edited the two gates start measuring
84	different things.
85	
86	Pass the configuration file explicitly on every invocation
87	(`--configuration=infection.json5`). Infection otherwise picks the first file it
88	finds from `infection.json5`, `infection.json`, `infection.json5.dist`,
89	`infection.json.dist`, so an unrelated file dropped into the project root can
90	silently take over the gate.
91	
92	`mutation-job.yml` contains `REPLACE_WITH_*` sentinels for the target's selected
93	tool runtime, extensions, and lock policy. Replace all of them before merging the
94	job; none is a default supplied by this repository.
95	
96	Replace `REPLACE_WITH_PRODUCTION_SOURCE_ROOT` in `infection.json5` with all target
97	production roots that should be mutated. Confirm the run generates mutants from
98	each root.
99	
100	Put the whole-tree baseline in the file and the changed-lines bar on the command
101	line. Pass `--ignore-msi-with-no-mutations` with the changed-lines flags rather than
102	setting `ignoreMsiWithNoMutations` in the file: a change that mutates nothing must
103	not score 0%, but a whole-tree run that generates nothing is a misconfiguration and
104	should fail rather than pass silently.
105	
106	Check `vendor/bin/infection --version` and validate the shipped configuration
107	against that installed release before copying version-specific keys. Configure the
108	newest resolved line first. When a target genuinely resolves an older line, consult
109	that line's schema and apply its documented spelling or limitation deliberately; a
110	schema-invalid file is not a cross-version configuration, and the template's own
111	lock resolution is not evidence about the target.
112	
113	## Why Two Thresholds
114	
115	Infection reports two scores:
116	
117	- **MSI** — detected mutants over all mutants, including mutants in code no test
118	  covers. Infection's default detected count includes killed, errored, and
119	  timed-out mutants. It answers "how much of the source is verified".
120	- **Covered MSI** — detected mutants over the mutants in covered code only. It answers
121	  "where tests do run, do they assert anything".
122	
123	A measured score describes the current suite; it does not define an acceptable
124	suite. The toolkit therefore supplies fixed minimums. Adoption includes paying
125	down enough weak tests and design debt to reach them rather than lowering the gate
126	to the score that happened to be measured.
127	
128	| Scope | Where the numbers live | `minMsi` | `minCoveredMsi` | Why |
129	|-------|------------------------|----------|-----------------|-----|
130	| Whole source tree | `infection.json5` | 80 | 80 | Fixed toolkit policy for the complete production tree |
131	| Changed lines | `--min-msi` / `--min-covered-msi` in CI | 85 | 85 | Fixed toolkit policy for new code |
132	
133	## Setting the Thresholds
134	
135	The shipped 80/80 whole-tree and 85/85 changed-lines values are fixed policy, not
136	placeholders or measurements.
137	
138	1. Run the gate with the thresholds neutralised:
139	
140	   ```bash
141	   vendor/bin/infection --configuration=infection.json5 --threads=max --min-msi=0 --min-covered-msi=0
142	   ```
143	
144	2. If either whole-tree score is below 80, keep the template unchanged and fix the
145	   suite and production design until both pass. The adoption is incomplete while
146	   the default branch cannot meet the baseline.
147	3. Read `build/infection/per-mutator.md` and
148	   `build/infection/escaped.log`. Add assertions for observable behavior first.
149	   When equivalent mutants cluster around an implementation idiom, improve that
150	   design instead of treating every survivor as permanent. Optional constructor
151	   injection such as `$this->x = $x ?? new X()` is a common example: prefer explicit
152	   construction or required dependencies when the fallback exists only for test
153	   convenience.
154	4. If the project already exceeds a floor, keep the shipped threshold. Record the
155	   measured result as evidence that the gate is feasible, not as a new policy.
156	   Tighten a threshold only when a human explicitly chooses that quality policy;
157	   do not derive it by rounding a single run.
158	5. Pass `--ignore-msi-with-no-mutations` on the changed-lines run. A pull request
159	   that touches only documentation, tests, or configuration produces no mutants, and
160	   a scoreless run must not be reported as 0%.
161	6. Re-measure after changes, but never rewrite policy from the measurement. A
162	   later threshold change remains an explicit human decision.
163	
164	Lowering a threshold to make a red build green defeats the gate. So does disabling a
165	mutator, widening `source.excludes`, or pointing the gate at fewer directories. Fix
166	the tests, and ask a human operator when an exception is genuinely justified.
167	
168	## Mutators
169	
170	Keep `"@default": true`. The default profile is what the published mutation scores
171	of other projects mean, and a trimmed profile makes the number incomparable and
172	usually flatters the suite.
173	
174	Resist disabling a mutator that produces equivalent mutants when it also kills real
175	ones. `Coalesce` still catches genuine missing tests on `??` over data even when a
176	particular construction idiom produces equivalent survivors. Improve that idiom;
177	disable a mutator only when it produces nothing but equivalent mutants for the
178	project, with human approval.
179	
180	## Analysis Scope
181	
182	Mutate production source only:
183	
184	```json5
185	"source": {
186	    "directories": ["REPLACE_WITH_PRODUCTION_SOURCE_ROOT"]
187	}
188	```
189	
190	`source.excludes` entries are relative to each source directory, not to the project
191	root. Resolve every path from the target's selected source directories.
192	
193	An exclusion needs a specific scope reason: for example, code tested only under a
194	different supported runtime, or reference declarations whose correctness is
195	established against an independent native parser and whose unit tests would merely
196	duplicate the declarations. Keep algorithms that interpret that data in scope.
197	Identify the exact files and independent check; a large array or surviving mutants
198	alone do not justify exclusion. Preserve an already authorized exception and ask
199	only when a new mutation-scope decision remains unresolved.
200	
201	## Timeouts
202	
203	Keep Infection's default timeout classification: timed-out mutants count as
204	detected. Loop-condition mutations can create infinite loops. Do not add
205	`timeoutsAsEscaped`, `maxTimeouts`, or a zero-timeout post-check unless the project
206	explicitly chooses that different policy.
207	
208	`timeout` is an operational value. Measure the covered initial suite and the
209	largest selected test set, then allow runner headroom. Infection may skip mutants
210	before execution when their estimated test duration exceeds the timeout; those
211	skips are distinct from mutants that ran and timed out. A green score with skipped
212	whole-tree mutants does not establish the baseline. Check `stats.skippedCount` in
213	the JSON report and fail the whole-tree gate when it is non-zero. Re-measure after
214	suite growth rather than retaining the first working timeout.
215	
216	Bound the PHP memory available to mutant test processes so warning floods or
217	runaway allocation terminate. Setting `php -d` on Infection's controller alone
218	does not establish the worker limit; configure the job's PHP INI and verify the
219	child processes. Size the controller/report reader separately for large reports.
220	
221	## Coverage Collection
222	
223	Keep `tmpDir` separate from the report directory in `logs`: Infection removes its
224	temporary directory when the run finishes.
225	
226	Let Infection run its normal initial test phase and generate the coverage it needs.
227	With pcov or Xdebug enabled, no separate PHPUnit coverage command is required.
228	`--coverage` means reuse an existing XML and JUnit report; it is not a prerequisite
229	for mutation testing. `--skip-initial-tests` is only valid when that existing report
230	is supplied and the suite was already proved green.
231	
232	Use `--only-covering-test-cases` for both gates when the installed release supports
233	it. This selects the tests covering each mutant without narrowing mutation scope.
234	
235	Do not add a `Generate coverage for mutation testing` step solely for Infection,
236	and do not pass `--coverage` or `--skip-initial-tests` in the standard job. Reuse a
237	pre-generated report only when the workflow already creates it for another
238	independent consumer and the saved runtime justifies the extra coupling.
239	
240	Keep `"testFrameworkExtraArgs": "--no-extensions"` so the toolkit's AI reporter
241	cannot replace the PHPUnit result output Infection reads to distinguish killed from
242	escaped mutants. A risky or failing initial test should fail the mutation job; do
243	not weaken PHPUnit with `--do-not-fail-on-risky`.
244	
245	`testFrameworkExtraArgs` arrived in Infection 0.34. On an older line the same value
246	goes under `testFrameworkOptions`, which every version from 0.26 accepts and 0.34
247	and later still honour; setting both is an error.
248	
249	## Do Not Wrap It in Composer Scripts
250	
251	Write the commands into the workflow. This gate runs in CI, so a Composer script
252	would add a layer to look through, a second place for the flags to drift from the
253	job that actually runs them, and Composer's 300-second process timeout to work
254	around — a mutation run on a suite of any size takes longer than that, and the
255	script dies partway through with a process timeout instead of a score.
256	
257	Composer scripts earn their place when a command is run by hand on every save, like
258	`composer lint`. Mutation testing is not that command, and it does not belong inside
259	`composer lint` either: those gates are seconds, this one is minutes.
260	
261	Do not explain this tooling in the target project's product `docs/` or rewrite its
262	README or `AGENTS.md`. The workflow and this vendor skill are the development
263	documentation unless the user explicitly names another developer-owned location.
264	
265	## CI Wiring
266	
267	Merge `mutation-job.yml` into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as a separate job. It needs
268	three things the other jobs do not:
269	
270	- `fetch-depth: 0` on checkout, so the pull request can be diffed against its base.
271	- A coverage driver: `coverage: pcov` in `setup-php`.
272	- A branch on the event: a changed-lines step guarded by
273	  `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, a whole-tree step guarded by the
274	  negation.
275	
276	Use the highest PHP version in the target's supported matrix for this one-off job,
277	not the template's literal version. Derive its extensions from Composer platform
278	requirements and the commands in the job, require the selected lock file to exist,
279	and run `composer check-platform-reqs` after installation. Treat job timeout,
280	memory limits, and `--threads` as measured operational values: size them from the
281	observed run and runner capacity without altering mutation scope or thresholds.
282	
283	In a monorepo, set the package working directory and verify a known changed source
284	line is selected. Set artifact upload paths relative to the repository root;
285	`defaults.run.working-directory` does not change an action's paths. Consult the
286	installed Infection release's Git diff path handling;
287	do not carry an old `diff.relative` workaround into a release that handles
288	repository-relative paths natively. Upload mutation reports even when a gate fails.
289	If manual whole-tree runs are provided, include the event name in concurrency keys
290	so dispatching one does not cancel a PR check on the same branch.
291	
292	Take the base branch from `origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}` rather than hardcoding the
293	default branch. GitHub sets that variable on pull request events, so a pull request
294	against a release branch is scored against that branch. Read it as a shell
295	environment variable rather than through `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}`
296	interpolation: a branch name pasted into the shell as literal text is a script
297	injection waiting to happen.
298	
299	## Protecting the Configuration
300	
301	Mutation thresholds are the first thing an agent lowers when a build goes red, so
302	treat these files the way the project treats its other non-negotiable configuration:
303	
304	- Recommend protecting `infection.json5` in the agent permission system. Do not
305	  edit `.claude/settings.json`, `AGENTS.md`, or another agent-owned policy file
306	  unless the user explicitly asks for that change.
307	- Add the file to `.gitattributes` with `export-ignore` if the project excludes dev
308	  configuration from its distributed archive.
309	- Keep `ForbiddenCommentRule` enabled. It rejects `@infection-ignore-all`, which is
310	  the other way to make a mutant disappear without writing a test.
311	
312	## Verification
313	
314	Run the two local commands above, or push the branch and read the job. Exit codes:
315	
316	- `0`: every threshold met
317	- Non-zero: a threshold was missed, or Infection could not run
318	
319	Read `build/infection/escaped.log` for the mutants that survived and
320	`build/infection/per-mutator.md` for the mutators they came from. Each escaped
321	mutant is a diff showing a change to production code that no test objected to;
322	write the test that objects.
323	
324	## References
325	
326	- [Infection documentation](https://infection.github.io/guide/) — Mutators, loggers, and CLI options.
327	- [ForbiddenCommentRule](vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/docs/rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md) — Why `@infection-ignore-all` is rejected.
328

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-github-actions
3	description: >-
4	  Set up GitHub Actions CI for php-ai-toolkit PHP projects. Use when asked to
5	  create or update .github/workflows/ci.yml, run toolkit checks in CI, pin
6	  GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs, align CI with supported PHP versions,
7	  harden workflow permissions and concurrency for Composer, PHPUnit, ParaTest,
8	  PHPStan, PHP-CS-Fixer, PHPCompatibility, LocGuard, TreeGuard, and Deptrac, or
9	  refresh the Context7 documentation index when the default branch, a tag, or
10	  a release changes.
11	---
12	
13	# Setup GitHub Actions CI
14	
15	This skill configures GitHub Actions so every php-ai-toolkit gate is visible in
16	CI and the workflow follows Actions security and maintainability practices.
17	
18	## Discover Project Constraints
19	
20	Read these files before editing CI:
21	
22	- `composer.json`: `require.php`, `config.platform.php`, and Composer scripts.
23	- Existing `.github/workflows/*.yml` or `.yaml`.
24	- Toolkit configs that imply CI gates: `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php`,
25	  `phpstan.neon`, `phpcs.xml.dist`, `loc.yaml`, `tree.yaml`, `deptrac.yaml`,
26	  `phpunit.xml.dist`.
27	- Project docs that declare supported PHP versions.
28	- Composer lock policy: one normal `composer.lock`, no committed lock, or
29	  PHP-versioned locks such as `composer.lock.php-<minor>`.
30	- Composer platform requirements and each command's runtime needs. Derive the
31	  `setup-php` extension list from `composer check-platform-reqs` plus the
32	  config-driven needs below; do not rely on what `ubuntu-latest` happens to
33	  preinstall, and do not copy another project's list.
34	
35	Extensions that a project's configuration demands even though no `require`
36	declares them:
37	
38	| Extension | Needed by | Failure without it |
39	|-----------|-----------|--------------------|
40	| `mbstring` | `phpunit/phpunit` and `infection/infection` require it directly | `composer install` fails the platform check |
41	| `pcntl` | `phpunit/php-invoker`, which implements PHPUnit's `enforceTimeLimit="true"` | Time limits are not enforced; PHPUnit 10+ raises a runner warning that `failOnAllIssues="true"` turns into exit 1 |
42	| `pcov` or Xdebug | Coverage and mutation testing | No coverage data |
43	| GD with FreeType | DocGen social preview images | Image generation fails |
44	
45	ParaTest does not need `pcntl`: it starts workers through `symfony/process`, and
46	its own `ext-pcntl` entry is a `require-dev` for its own test suite.
47	
48	Apply the list to every job that installs the dev graph or runs tests, including a
49	mutation-testing job — it executes the same `phpunit.xml.dist` through Infection
50	and hits the same requirements as the test job.
51	
52	If the declared PHP floor, Composer constraint, docs, and CI matrix disagree,
53	surface the conflict and make CI match the declared support policy.
54	
55	## Template
56	
57	Read the template from
58	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-github-actions/ci.yml`
59	and apply it to the project root as `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
60	
61	The template contains `REPLACE_WITH_*` sentinels instead of this repository's PHP
62	matrix and lock policy. Replace every sentinel from target-project evidence before
63	installing the workflow; a remaining sentinel is a failed setup, not a default.
64	
65	If a workflow already exists, merge rather than blindly replacing it.
66	
67	## Required CI Gates
68	
69	The workflow must make the toolkit checks observable as separate named steps.
70	Do not hide all lint gates behind a single unnamed `composer lint` step.
71	
72	Required gates when the corresponding script/config exists:
73	
74	- `composer format:check` for PHP-CS-Fixer.
75	- `composer phpstan` for PHPStan and toolkit PHPStan rules.
76	- `composer compat` for PHPCompatibility.
77	- `composer loc-guard` for LocGuard.
78	- `composer tree-guard` for TreeGuard.
79	- `composer deptrac` for Deptrac.
80	- `composer test` for the PHPUnit suite when ParaTest is installed, otherwise
81	  `composer test:unit`.
82	
83	Property-based tests configured by `/setup-toolkit-pbt` run through
84	`composer test:pbt` in their separate `pbt.yml` workflow. Verify that workflow is
85	present and that ordinary PHPUnit and ParaTest commands exclude the `pbt` group;
86	do not add the slower group to the normal test matrix as well.
87	
88	Every gate the project has configured belongs in CI. A tool that is installed,
89	configured, and wired into `composer lint` but never runs on the default branch
90	is a gate the project believes it has: it passes locally for whoever last ran it
91	and drifts from then on. When a config file exists and its Composer script does
92	not run anywhere in CI, that is the finding to report, not a detail to leave.
93	
94	Keep `compat` inside the `lint` job alongside formatting, PHPStan, LocGuard,
95	TreeGuard, and Deptrac. It may be a separate step for visibility, but it should
96	not be a separate CI job unless the project has an explicit reason. Namespace
97	visibility is enforced by the toolkit's PHPStan rules and needs no separate CI
98	step.
99	
100	If a script is missing but the config exists, add the Composer script using the
101	corresponding setup skill before wiring CI. If neither script nor config exists,
102	do not invent the gate in CI; set up that tool first.
103	
104	### The Parallel Test Runner
105	
106	When ParaTest is installed, make `composer test` select it and run that command in
107	the normal PHP matrix. Do not add a second sequential PHPUnit job: ParaTest already
108	executes the PHPUnit suite, and the matrix simultaneously verifies runtime support
109	and isolation across worker processes.
110	
111	A real multi-major matrix must use the version-selecting `tests/run.php` runner from
112	`/setup-toolkit-phpunit`, so ParaTest receives the configuration matching the
113	installed PHPUnit major. Do not rely on the newest `phpunit.xml.dist` under older
114	dependency graphs. Keep `composer test:unit` available for local debugging and for
115	tools that specifically require PHPUnit, but CI does not need to repeat it.
116	
117	## Separate Decision: Documentation Publishing
118	
119	Do not add documentation generation or GitHub Pages publishing to `ci.yml`.
120	Those live in their own workflows, and their templates and the questions to ask
121	before installing them belong to the `/setup-toolkit-docgen` skill.
122	
123	Do not silently finish when the project has a `docgen` script but no DocGen
124	workflow. Ask the user to choose one of the three supported outcomes: local only,
125	publish the default branch, or publish the default branch plus pull-request diff
126	previews. Then use `/setup-toolkit-docgen` for the chosen workflows. The workflows
127	remain separate from `ci.yml` so publishing permissions do not leak into CI.
128	
129	## Separate Decision: Context7 Documentation Refresh
130	
131	Context7 (https://context7.com) indexes a repository's documentation and serves
132	it to AI coding agents. It re-indexes public libraries on its own schedule, so a
133	project that wants agents to read current documentation asks for a refresh from
134	a workflow. Keep that workflow separate from `ci.yml`: the API key is a secret,
135	and `ci.yml` runs untrusted pull-request code.
136	
137	Do not install it unasked. When the target publishes documentation that agents
138	are expected to consume, ask the user whether the library is registered on
139	Context7 and which event should refresh it. Two things must exist before the
140	workflow can succeed, and neither can be created from the repository:
141	
142	1. The library page at `https://context7.com/<owner>/<repository>`. If it does
143	   not exist, the user adds the repository at https://context7.com/add-library.
144	2. The `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` repository secret, copied from
145	   https://context7.com/dashboard into Settings > Secrets and variables >
146	   Actions.
147	
148	Read the template from
149	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-github-actions/context7.yml`
150	and apply it as `.github/workflows/context7.yml`. It sends one request to
151	`POST https://context7.com/api/v1/refresh` and needs no checkout, PHP, or
152	Composer step; do not add them, and do not replace the request with a
153	third-party action.
154	
155	Choose the trigger from the lifecycle the documentation follows. The template
156	refreshes on every push to the default branch; replace
157	`REPLACE_WITH_DEFAULT_BRANCH` for that case and swap the `on` block for the
158	others. Keep `workflow_dispatch` in every variant so a refresh can be requested
159	by hand.
160	
161	| Consumers read | Trigger |
162	|----------------|---------|
163	| The default branch: trunk-based development, VCS installs, or a documentation site built from it | `push` to the default branch, as in the template |
164	| Tagged versions | `push` on tags matching the project's version pattern |
165	| GitHub releases | `release` with type `published` |
166	
167	```yaml
168	on:
169	  push:
170	    tags:
171	      - 'v*'
172	  workflow_dispatch:
173	```
174	
175	```yaml
176	on:
177	  release:
178	    types:
179	      - published
180	  workflow_dispatch:
181	```
182	
183	The request re-indexes the branch Context7 tracks, which is the default branch
184	unless the library was registered otherwise. A tag or release trigger therefore
185	publishes whatever that branch holds when the event fires; it does not index the
186	tag itself. Add `branch` to the request body only when Context7 already tracks
187	that branch, because the API answers `branch_not_found` otherwise.
188	
189	`libraryName` is `/<owner>/<repository>`, which the template derives from
190	`github.repository`. Replace it with a literal only when the Context7 library id
191	differs from the GitHub name, such as after a repository rename. Private
192	repositories need a paid Context7 plan and a `gitToken` in the request; report
193	that requirement instead of adding a second secret unprompted.
194	
195	Context7 indexes markdown-family files from the tracked branch and falls back to
196	source files when a repository has no documentation. If generated output,
197	fixtures, or vendored documentation would pollute the index, a `context7.json`
198	at the repository root narrows the scope; see
199	https://context7.com/docs/adding-libraries for the current fields.
200	
201	Context7 accepts a refresh of a library at most once per minimum interval, ten
202	days at the time of writing, and answers `400` with `"error":"too-early"` in
203	between. The template treats that answer as a skipped refresh: it annotates the
204	run and exits successfully, because the next push after the interval refreshes
205	the library and a red badge would report a non-defect. Every other error still
206	fails the job. If pushes are rare enough that a declined refresh may not be
207	followed by another push for weeks, a `schedule` trigger at the interval's
208	cadence catches up; add it only when the user confirms the tracked branch should
209	be re-indexed without a push.
210	
211	After installing the workflow, validate it with actionlint. Once the secret
212	exists, run it through `workflow_dispatch` and read the job log:
213	
214	- `{"message":"Refresh started successfully"}`: the refresh is queued.
215	- `400` with `too-early`: the interval since the last update has not passed;
216	  the job exits 0 with a notice, and the answer proves the secret and the
217	  library id work.
218	- `401`: the secret is missing or wrong.
219	- `404`: the library is not registered, or `libraryName` differs from its id.
220	- `429`: refreshes are rate limited; do not add retries to work around it.
221	
222	## Out of Scope: Mutation Testing
223	
224	Do not write a mutation testing job from scratch. `/setup-toolkit-infection` ships
225	the job together with the configuration it depends on, because the job needs a
226	coverage driver, `fetch-depth: 0`, and different direct Infection arguments per
227	event. Use that skill when an Infection job is in scope.
228	
229	## Out of Scope: Performance Benchmarks
230	
231	Do not add PHPBench to the normal test or lint matrix. `/setup-toolkit-phpbench`
232	owns the benchmark contract, stable runner settings, paired merge-target and
233	candidate measurements, and any requested comparison gate. Preserve an existing
234	standalone benchmark job when applying CI conventions; do not replace it with a
235	new comparison workflow unless that capability is requested. A single execution
236	is not evidence of performance relative to the base revision.
237	
238	## Out of Scope: Fuzzing
239	
240	Do not write a generic fuzz job in `ci.yml`. `/setup-toolkit-fuzzing` derives the
241	input generator and oracle from a specific contract and ships a separate scheduled
242	workflow with corpus caching and crash artifacts. A random-input loop without that
243	contract design is not a CI gate.
244	
245	## PHP Version Coverage
246	
247	CI must match the project's declared support range. Do not compensate for a
248	bad Composer constraint by narrowing the workflow matrix.
249	
250	1. Determine the supported PHP range from `composer.json require.php` and the
251	   project docs.
252	2. List every supported minor version in the `tests` matrix.
253	3. Prefer the project's existing lock policy. A normal single `composer.lock`
254	   is fine for most applications. Use PHP-versioned lock files only when a
255	   supported older PHP minor needs a different dependency graph and the project
256	   has a supply-chain requirement to pin those graphs, which is common for
257	   libraries and developer tools.
258	4. If the project uses PHP-versioned lock files, make sure every matrix minor
259	   has a matching `composer.lock.php-<minor>` file.
260	5. Check whether dev dependencies can install on each minor:
261	   ```bash
262	   cp "composer.lock.php-<minor>" composer.lock
263	   composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
264	   ```
265	6. If dependencies do not install on a supported PHP minor, fix the Composer
266	   constraints first. Select the newest compatible tool line for that leg and add
267	   an older line only when Composer proves the target matrix needs it.
268	7. Run the lint gates as named steps in one `lint` job on the highest supported
269	   runtime compatible with the tooling. PHPCompatibility checks the declared PHP
270	   range; repeating formatting, PHPStan, LocGuard, TreeGuard, and Deptrac on every
271	   runtime adds no distinct gate.
272	8. Use the highest matrix minor for one-off mutation, documentation, and benchmark
273	   jobs unless the tool cannot run there. Record that limitation rather than
274	   copying the template's PHP literal.
275	
276	Never use `--ignore-platform-reqs` to make a lower PHP job pass. That hides a
277	real compatibility problem.
278	
279	Check upper PHP bounds in the locked dev graph as well as minimum versions.
280	`composer check-platform-reqs --no-dev` verifies product requirements only; it
281	cannot establish that ParaTest or another development tool supports that runtime.
282	If resolving the mismatch requires changing an intentional dependency policy
283	outside the CI request, report that limitation explicitly instead of claiming the
284	green test job proves full platform compatibility.
285	
286	The workflow template is deliberately incomplete until its PHP values, test command,
287	extensions, branches, and lock steps are derived from the target. Never retain a
288	literal merely because it matches php-ai-toolkit's own CI. In particular, do not
289	copy this repository's full matrix or versioned-lock topology into a single-runtime
290	application.
291	
292	When generating PHP-versioned lock files, do not write `config.platform.php`
293	into the root `composer.json`. Repeat this process for each minor in the target's
294	actual support matrix, using a temporary directory and Composer home:
295	
296	```bash
297	target_php='<supported-minor>'
298	lock_tmp_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
299	composer_home_dir="$lock_tmp_dir/composer-home"
300	mkdir -p "$composer_home_dir"
301	cp composer.json "$lock_tmp_dir/composer.json"
302	COMPOSER_HOME="$composer_home_dir" composer --working-dir="$lock_tmp_dir" config -g platform.php "$target_php.0"
303	COMPOSER_HOME="$composer_home_dir" composer --working-dir="$lock_tmp_dir" update --no-install --no-audit --no-interaction --no-progress
304	cp "$lock_tmp_dir/composer.lock" "composer.lock.php-$target_php"
305	```
306	
307	## Actions Best Practices
308	
309	Apply these rules to every workflow created by this skill:
310	
311	- Pin every external action with the full 40-character commit SHA.
312	- Keep workflow YAML free of explanatory comments. Use clear job and step names.
313	- Verify each SHA from the action's original repository:
314	  ```bash
315	  gh release view --repo actions/checkout --json tagName,publishedAt,url
316	  git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/actions/checkout.git 'refs/tags/<tag>'
317	  ```
318	- Use top-level `permissions: contents: read` and only grant additional
319	  permissions for a step that truly needs them.
320	- Use `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`, for untrusted PR code.
321	- Use `concurrency` with PR number or ref and `cancel-in-progress: true`.
322	  Include the event name so a manual whole-tree mutation run cannot cancel the PR
323	  checks on the same branch.
324	- Set `fail-fast: false` for version matrices so all supported minors report.
325	- Add `timeout-minutes` to jobs.
326	- Give every job and every step a clear `name`.
327	- Do not use `continue-on-error` for required lint or test gates.
328	- When versioned lock files are used, copy the matching lock to `composer.lock`
329	  before validation and installation, then install with locked dependencies and
330	  `require-lock-file: true`. Run `composer check-platform-reqs` after installation.
331	- When no lock file is committed, do not claim `dependency-versions: locked` and
332	  do not set `require-lock-file: true`; deliberately install the dependency mode
333	  the project chose.
334	- Let `ramsey/composer-install` handle Composer caching; do not add a second
335	  Composer cache step unless the project has a measured reason.
336	
337	Job timeouts, PHP memory limits, and worker counts are operational starting
338	points. Measure sustained runtime, peak memory, and runner capacity, then adjust
339	them with headroom. Never use those settings to narrow a gate, skip targets, or
340	turn a quality failure into a pass. The template's values are not target-project
341	facts.
342	
343	## Updating Action Pins
344	
345	When refreshing the template, resolve current releases and SHAs before editing:
346	
347	```bash
348	gh release view --repo actions/checkout --json tagName,publishedAt,url
349	git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/actions/checkout.git 'refs/tags/<tag>'
350	
351	gh release view --repo shivammathur/setup-php --json tagName,publishedAt,url
352	git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/shivammathur/setup-php.git 'refs/tags/<tag>'
353	
354	gh release view --repo ramsey/composer-install --json tagName,publishedAt,url
355	git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/ramsey/composer-install.git 'refs/tags/<tag>'
356	```
357	
358	Use the SHA returned for the exact tag. Do not use a moving branch, a major tag,
359	or an abbreviated SHA.
360	
361	## Verification
362	
363	After editing the workflow:
364	
365	```bash
366	git diff --check
367	go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@latest .github/workflows/ci.yml
368	```
369	
370	Include `.github/workflows/context7.yml` in that command when the Context7
371	workflow was installed.
372	
373	Run local Composer checks that are reasonably available:
374	
375	```bash
376	composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
377	# Repeat validation with each target-project lock when versioned locks exist.
378	composer format:check
379	composer phpstan
380	composer compat
381	composer loc-guard
382	composer tree-guard
383	composer deptrac
384	composer test:unit
385	composer test
386	```
387	
388	Then check that nothing configured was left out of the workflow. Every Composer
389	script the project treats as a gate should appear in `ci.yml`:
390	
391	```bash
392	composer run-script --list
393	grep -o 'composer [a-z:-]*' .github/workflows/ci.yml | sort -u
394	```
395	
396	If a local check cannot run because of the local PHP version or missing tools,
397	state that clearly and rely on the CI job that covers it.
398	
399	## References
400	
401	- [GitHub Actions security hardening](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
402	- [GitHub Actions workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions)
403	- [Composer Install action](https://github.com/ramsey/composer-install)
404	- [Context7 GitHub Actions integration](https://context7.com/docs/integrations/github-actions)
405	- [Context7 refresh API](https://context7.com/docs/api-reference/refresh/refresh-a-library)
