1	---
2	name: setup-php-ai-toolkit
3	description: >-
4	  Set up php-ai-toolkit end to end in a PHP project by selecting and applying
5	  the relevant setup-toolkit component skills. Use for a complete toolkit setup;
6	  use the named component skill directly when the request concerns one tool only.
7	---
8	
9	# Set Up php-ai-toolkit
10	
11	This skill is the entry point for applying php-ai-toolkit to a user's project.
12	It coordinates the component setup skills; the component skills own the detailed
13	requirements, templates, and verification steps.
14	
15	## Inspect the Project
16	
17	Before selecting components, read:
18	
19	- `composer.json`, including PHP constraints, autoload roots, dependencies, and
20	  scripts;
21	- the source and test directory layout;
22	- existing tool configuration and GitHub Actions workflows; and
23	- the project's current diff so unrelated changes are preserved.
24	
25	Use values derived from the target project. Do not copy PHP versions, paths,
26	namespaces, dependency constraints, or CI settings from the php-ai-toolkit
27	repository.
28	
29	In a monorepo, identify the requested package and its owning workflows before
30	editing. Keep package commands, autoload changes, generated output, and tool
31	dependencies within that scope; update shared callers only where the change
32	requires it.
33	
34	Setup does not include rewriting the product README, adding architecture or
35	tooling pages under `docs/`, or creating `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Keep setup rationale in
36	the delivery explanation and operational settings in their tool files. If the user
37	requests a documentation edit, preserve content outside that request; removing a
38	section does not authorize replacing the rest of the README or moving the removed
39	material into a new guide.
40	
41	Preserve established tool and workflow layouts. Standardizing a component's
42	configuration does not by itself call for a new workflow or a nested Composer
43	project under `tools/`.
44	
45	## Apply Component Skills
46	
47	Read and follow the component skills in this order:
48	
49	1. `/setup-toolkit-phpstan`
50	2. `/setup-toolkit-phpunit` and `/setup-toolkit-doctest`
51	3. Assess performance-sensitive public operations and use
52	   `/setup-toolkit-phpbench` only when a stable representative workload can
53	   support a useful local benchmark or pull-request comparison
54	4. Assess the project's contracts and use `/setup-toolkit-pbt` and/or
55	   `/setup-toolkit-fuzzing` only where structured properties or coverage-guided
56	   exploration provide a meaningful oracle
57	5. `/setup-toolkit-php-cs-fixer` and `/setup-toolkit-php-compatibility`
58	6. `/setup-toolkit-loc-guard` and `/setup-toolkit-tree-guard`
59	7. `/setup-toolkit-deptrac`
60	8. `/setup-toolkit-infection`
61	9. `/setup-toolkit-docgen`
62	10. `/setup-toolkit-github-actions`
63	
64	Use `/setup-toolkit-agents-md` only when the user explicitly asks to create or
65	change `AGENTS.md`, and `/setup-toolkit-readme` only when the user explicitly
66	asks to create or change `README.md`.
67	
68	When multiple component skills update the same target file, combine their
69	requirements into that file. GitHub Actions is applied last so its jobs invoke the
70	commands and configuration selected by the other component skills.
71	
72	PHPBench, fuzzing, and PBT are not checkbox gates. Skip PHPBench when no stable
73	representative workload exists. Skip either fuzzing or PBT when no contract has a
74	generator and oracle strong enough to justify it, and report those decisions.
75	
76	The core adoption is incomplete until PHPStan, PHPUnit, PHP-CS-Fixer,
77	PHPCompatibility, LocGuard, TreeGuard, Deptrac, Infection, and GitHub Actions are
78	installed, configured, wired into Composer, and exercised. Doctest and DocGen are
79	also part of a complete adoption when the project has maintained PHPDoc examples or
80	published API documentation.
81	
82	Do not silently classify a core component as inapplicable. LocGuard and TreeGuard
83	apply to every project with maintained production PHP source. PHPCompatibility
84	applies whenever the project declares a PHP support range. Deptrac applies even to
85	a flat library: discover or create a meaningful responsibility boundary, and stop
86	for the project's architecture decision if one cannot be derived without guessing.
87	If a core component is genuinely blocked by the target's runtime or dependency
88	graph, report the exact blocker and leave the overall setup incomplete.
89	
90	Before applying GitHub Actions, verify this completion table against files and
91	Composer scripts rather than against work already attempted:
92	
93	| Component | Required evidence |
94	|-----------|-------------------|
95	| PHPStan | `phpstan.neon` or `.dist`, and `composer phpstan` |
96	| PHPUnit | version-correct configuration, and `composer test:unit` |
97	| PHP-CS-Fixer | `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php`, and `composer format:check` |
98	| PHPCompatibility | `phpcs.xml.dist`, and `composer compat` |
99	| LocGuard | `loc.yaml`, and `composer loc-guard` |
100	| TreeGuard | `tree.yaml`, and `composer tree-guard` |
101	| Deptrac | `deptrac.yaml`, and `composer deptrac` |
102	| Infection | `infection.json5`, and a mutation CI job |
103	
104	Every configured fast gate must also appear in the aggregate `lint` script. Re-open
105	the generated workflow after GitHub Actions is applied and confirm that every row
106	is invoked. Missing evidence is a setup failure, not an optional follow-up.
107

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-agents-md
3	description: >-
4	  Set up AGENTS.md with project conventions and AI agent guidelines for a PHP project.
5	  Use when asked to create AGENTS.md, set up AI agent guidelines, or configure project conventions for AI agents.
6	---
7	
8	# Setup AGENTS.md
9	
10	This skill creates an AGENTS.md file that provides context and rules for AI agents working on the project.
11	
12	Use this skill only when the user explicitly asks to create or change
13	`AGENTS.md`. Applying php-ai-toolkit, adding quality gates, or repairing project
14	architecture is not permission to edit agent instructions. If `AGENTS.md`
15	already exists, treat it as human-owned: inspect it for constraints, then ask
16	before changing even an outdated section.
17	
18	## What is AGENTS.md?
19	
20	AGENTS.md is a convention for providing AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) with project-specific context. It tells agents:
21	- What the project does
22	- What quality standards to follow
23	- How the codebase is organized
24	- Where to find documentation
25	
26	## Template
27	
28	Read the template from `vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-agents-md/AGENTS.md`.
29	
30	## Section Explanations
31	
32	### NOTE Comment
33	The `<!-- NOTE -->` comment at the top tells AI agents that this file is human-managed and should not be modified by agents. This prevents accidental overwrites.
34	
35	### Project Description
36	Replace `{{PROJECT_DESCRIPTION}}` with a description that covers:
37	
38	1. What the project does (1-3 sentences)
39	2. The project's goal — why it exists and what it is trying to achieve
40	3. Core concepts — key ideas or domain terms that AI agents need to understand to work on the project
41	
42	Write in prose, not bullet points. Example (from a dependency analysis CLI tool):
43	> A CLI tool that analyzes PHP code dependencies and visualizes the blast radius of changes. Its primary goal is impact analysis — automatically identifying what breaks when a class, method, or function changes. The tool builds a bidirectional graph model where nodes represent code elements (classes, methods, functions) and edges represent relationships (calls, extends, implements). Inverse edges are generated automatically, enabling traversal in both directions: what the target depends on, and what depends on the target. Output is available in two formats: a tree display for humans and structured data for AI agents.
44	
45	### Supported Versions
46	Replace `{{SUPPORTED_VERSIONS}}` with the compatibility guarantees that agents
47	need while changing the project. Determine them from `composer.json`, the CI
48	matrix, and project documentation, and list only versions the project explicitly
49	supports.
50	
51	Keep this section focused on the primary runtimes, platforms, frameworks, and
52	development tools whose versions materially affect project-wide changes. Do not
53	copy every direct or transitive package constraint from `composer.json`, and do not
54	list internal parser, adapter, or helper libraries merely because the project
55	supports multiple versions of them. Composer remains the source of truth for those
56	implementation dependencies.
57	
58	Write the target's real constraint or enumerated CI-supported minors. Do not copy
59	a version list from this repository. Shape example:
60	```markdown
61	- **PHP**: <versions guaranteed by this project>
62	```
63	
64	### Architecture
65	Replace `{{ARCHITECTURE}}` with a description of the project's layering and responsibility boundaries. This is NOT a directory listing — it describes how the layers relate to each other and what each layer is responsible for.
66	
67	Include:
68	1. A one-line pipeline or flow summary showing how data/control moves through the system
69	2. A table mapping each layer to its responsibility and key entry point
70	
71	Example (from a CLI tool):
72	```markdown
73	Pipeline: `CLI input → Config stacking → Action → Analyzer → Graph → Traversal → Reporter → output`
74	
75	| Layer | Responsibility | Key file |
76	|-------|---------------|----------|
77	| **Command** | IO only — parse arguments, delegate output | `src/Command/InspectCommand.php` |
78	| **Config** | Merge 4 layers: Default → Env → YAML → CLI | `src/Config/ConfigLoader.php` |
79	| **Action** | Orchestrate Analyzer and Reporter | `src/Action/Inspect/InspectAction.php` |
80	| **Analyzer** | Parse source code → build Graph | `src/Analyzer/` |
81	| **Reporter** | Format graph into output | `src/Reporter/` |
82	
83	Dependencies between layers flow top-down only. Command never calls Analyzer directly.
84	```
85	
86	### Document References
87	Replace `{{DOCUMENT_REFERENCES}}` with links to project-specific documentation
88	directly under `docs/`. Keep this section as a short index of top-level entry
89	points; do not list files from nested directories such as `docs/rules/`. Detailed
90	pages should be linked from the relevant top-level document instead. Example:
91	```markdown
92	- [API Specification](docs/api-spec.md)
93	- [Database Schema](docs/schema.md)
94	```
95	
96	If the project has no documentation directly under `docs/`, remove this section
97	entirely.
98	
99	## Adaptation Workflow
100	
101	When applying this template to a project, follow these steps:
102	
103	1. **Read `composer.json`** to determine the primary supported runtimes and tools
104	2. **Scan the directory structure** to understand project layout
105	3. **Look for top-level documentation** directly under `docs/`
106	4. **Fill in all `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` values** with real project information
107	5. **Remove unused placeholders and sections**
108	6. **Place as `AGENTS.md`** in the project root only after confirming that no
109	   existing file will be overwritten
110	
111	## Protecting AGENTS.md
112	
113	After creating AGENTS.md, recommend setting up `.claude/settings.json` to prevent AI agents from modifying it. Do not edit an existing settings file unless the user explicitly asks:
114	
115	```json
116	{
117	    "permissions": {
118	        "deny": [
119	            "Edit(/AGENTS.md)",
120	            "Bash(*AGENTS.md*)"
121	        ]
122	    }
123	}
124	```
125	
126	Create `CLAUDE.md` only when the user explicitly asks for Claude-specific setup:
127	
128	```markdown
129	<!-- NOTE: You do not have permission to overwrite this file. Please ask a human operator to perform the changes for you. -->
130	@AGENTS.md
131	```
132

1	name: Fuzz (ztd-query-mysql)
2	
3	on:
4	  schedule:
5	    - cron: '0 2 * * *'
6	  workflow_dispatch:
7	    inputs:
8	      max_runs:
9	        description: Maximum inputs evaluated by each fuzz target after the seed corpus is replayed
10	        required: true
11	        default: '1000'
12	        type: string
13	
14	permissions:
15	  contents: read
16	
17	concurrency:
18	  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
19	  cancel-in-progress: false
20	
21	env:
22	  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
23	
24	jobs:
25	  fuzz:
26	    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
27	    name: Fuzz ${{ matrix.target.name }}
28	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
29	    timeout-minutes: 45
30	    permissions:
31	      contents: read
32	      issues: write
33	    strategy:
34	      fail-fast: false
35	      matrix:
36	        target:
37	          - name: behavior
38	            script: fuzz/fuzz_behavior.php
39	            corpus: fuzz/corpus/behavior
40	            fixtures: '0'
41	            extensions: pdo, pdo_mysql, dom, filter, hash, iconv, json, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, pcre, phar, reflection, simplexml, spl, tokenizer, xml, xmlwriter
42	          - name: fixtures
43	            script: fuzz/fuzz_behavior.php
44	            corpus: fuzz/corpus/fixtures
45	            fixtures: '1'
46	            extensions: pdo, pdo_mysql, dom, filter, hash, iconv, json, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, pcre, phar, reflection, simplexml, spl, tokenizer, xml, xmlwriter
47	    defaults:
48	      run:
49	        working-directory: packages/ztd-query-mysql
50	    steps:
51	      - name: Check out the repository
52	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
53	
54	      - name: Set up PHP
55	        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
56	        with:
57	          php-version: '8.5'
58	          extensions: ${{ matrix.target.extensions }}
59	          coverage: none
60	
61	      - name: Validate the Composer manifest and lock file
62	        run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
63	
64	      - name: Install dependencies
65	        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
66	        with:
67	          working-directory: packages/ztd-query-mysql
68	          dependency-versions: locked
69	          composer-options: --prefer-dist
70	          require-lock-file: true
71	
72	      - name: Check runtime platform requirements
73	        run: composer check-platform-reqs --no-dev
74	
75	      - name: Validate the manual run budget
76	        env:
77	          FUZZ_MAX_RUNS: ${{ inputs.max_runs || '1000' }}
78	        run: |
79	          case "$FUZZ_MAX_RUNS" in
80	            ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 'max_runs must be a positive integer.' >&2; exit 2 ;;
81	          esac
82	          if [ "${#FUZZ_MAX_RUNS}" -gt 8 ] || [ "$FUZZ_MAX_RUNS" -lt 1 ]; then
83	            echo 'max_runs must be between 1 and 99999999.' >&2
84	            exit 2
85	          fi
86	
87	      - name: Restore the evolving corpus
88	        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
89	        with:
90	          path: packages/ztd-query-mysql/${{ matrix.target.corpus }}
91	          key: ztd-query-mysql-corpus-v3-${{ matrix.target.name }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
92	          restore-keys: ztd-query-mysql-corpus-v3-${{ matrix.target.name }}-
93	
94	      - name: Run PHP-Fuzzer
95	        env:
96	          FUZZ_MAX_RUNS: ${{ inputs.max_runs || '1000' }}
97	          FUZZ_SCRIPT: ${{ matrix.target.script }}
98	          FUZZ_CORPUS: ${{ matrix.target.corpus }}
99	          FUZZ_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target.name }}
100	          ZTD_FUZZ_FIXTURES: ${{ matrix.target.fixtures }}
101	        run: |
102	          set -euo pipefail
103	          mkdir -p build/fuzz "$FUZZ_CORPUS"
104	          if [ "$ZTD_FUZZ_FIXTURES" = '0' ]; then
105	            cp ../sql-faker/seeds/mysql/mysql-8.4.7/* "$FUZZ_CORPUS/"
106	          fi
107	          php -d memory_limit=-1 vendor/bin/php-fuzzer fuzz \
108	            "$FUZZ_SCRIPT" \
109	            "$FUZZ_CORPUS/" \
110	            "--max-runs=$FUZZ_MAX_RUNS" --timeout=60 2>&1 | tee "build/fuzz/$FUZZ_TARGET.log"
111	
112	      - name: Open an issue for a finding
113	        uses: actions/github-script@ed597411d8f924073f98dfc5c65a23a2325f34cd
114	        env:
115	          FUZZ_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target.name }}
116	          FUZZ_SCRIPT: ${{ matrix.target.script }}
117	          ZTD_FUZZ_FIXTURES: ${{ matrix.target.fixtures }}
118	        with:
119	          script: |

28	            split_repository: bison-parser

30	            split_repository: lemon-parser

35	          - local_path: sql-parser
36	            split_repository: sql-parser

38	            split_repository: sql-formatter
39	          - local_path: sql-semantics

41	          - local_path: sql-semantics-mysql

43	          - local_path: sql-semantics-postgres
44	            split_repository: sql-semantics-postgres
45	          - local_path: sql-semantics-sqlite
46	            split_repository: sql-semantics-sqlite
47	          - local_path: sql-catalog
48	            split_repository: sql-catalog
49	          - local_path: requirements

51	          - local_path: ztd-query-mysql
52	            split_repository: ztd-query-mysql
53	          - local_path: ztd-query-postgres
54	            split_repository: ztd-query-postgres
55	          - local_path: ztd-query-sqlite
56	            split_repository: ztd-query-sqlite
57	          - local_path: ztd-query-pdo-adapter
58	            split_repository: ztd-query-pdo-adapter
59	          - local_path: ztd-query-mysqli-adapter

63	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

66	        id: version
67	        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')

3	# Core concepts have no dependencies on the three independent platforms.
4	# Layers follow the life of a parse table: a grammar is read from its upstream
5	# source, compiled into an LALR(1) automaton, stored as a table, and driven at
6	# runtime by a lexer and the parser. Each dialect composes those stages.
7	deptrac:
8	  paths:
9	    - ./src
10	  analyser:
11	    types:
12	      - class
13	      - use
14	  layers:
15	    # Symbols, rules and precedences as a grammar declares them.
16	    - name: Grammar
17	      collectors:
18	        - type: directory
19	          value: 'src/Grammar/'
20	    # Turns the trees of bison-parser and lemon-parser into grammars.
21	    - name: Compiler
22	      collectors:
23	        - type: directory
24	          value: 'src/Compiler/'
25	    # The lossless Bison grammar tree, from the bison-parser package.
26	    - name: BisonParser
27	      collectors:
28	        - type: classNameRegex
29	          value: '/^BisonParser\\/'
30	    # The lossless Lemon grammar tree, from the lemon-parser package.
31	    - name: LemonParser
32	      collectors:
33	        - type: classNameRegex
34	          value: '/^LemonParser\\/'
35	    # Builds the LALR(1) automaton and resolves its conflicts into a table.
36	    - name: Automaton
37	      collectors:
38	        - type: directory
39	          value: 'src/Automaton/'
40	    # The parse table as it is stored, loaded and consulted.
41	    - name: Table
42	      collectors:
43	        - type: directory
44	          value: 'src/Table/'
45	    # Tokens and the cursor the dialect lexers read with.
46	    - name: Lexer
47	      collectors:
48	        - type: directory
49	          value: 'src/Lexer/'
50	    # Drives a table over tokens and builds the syntax tree.
51	    - name: Parser
52	      collectors:
53	        - type: directory
54	          value: 'src/Parser/'
55	    # Names the releases each dialect ships tables for.
56	    - name: Resource
57	      collectors:
58	        - type: directory
59	          value: 'src/Resource/'
60	    - name: MySql
61	      collectors:
62	        - type: directory
63	          value: 'src/MySql/'
64	    - name: PostgreSql
65	      collectors:
66	        - type: directory
67	          value: 'src/PostgreSql/'
68	    - name: Sqlite
69	      collectors:
70	        - type: directory
71	          value: 'src/Sqlite/'

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-pbt
3	description: >-
4	  Set up property-based testing with Eris in a PHP project, including
5	  domain-specific generators, shrinkable properties, reproducible seeds, PHPUnit
6	  group isolation, dedicated Composer commands, and a separate GitHub Actions
7	  workflow. Use when structured inputs and invariants are a better fit than
8	  coverage-guided byte fuzzing.
9	---
10	
11	# Set Up Property-Based Testing with Eris
12	
13	Property-based testing (PBT) verifies a contract over many generated structured
14	values and shrinks a failure to a smaller counterexample. It is not a replacement
15	for examples, and an iteration loop around random Faker values is not PBT unless
16	the generator, property, shrinking, and reproduction behavior are intentional.
17	
18	## Inspect and Choose the Contract
19	
20	Read `composer.json`, PHP and PHPUnit constraints, every lock and PHPUnit
21	configuration, current unit/integration scripts, coverage metadata policy, source
22	contracts, and existing generators or random tests.
23	
24	Use PBT when the important claim can be expressed over structured values, for
25	example:
26	
27	- encode/decode or parse/render round trips;
28	- idempotence and canonicalization;
29	- algebraic behavior that the product actually promises;
30	- equivalence with a small reference model or alternate implementation;
31	- invariants before and after a command sequence; or
32	- boundary-rich validation where Eris can shrink to a useful value.
33	
34	Use `/setup-toolkit-fuzzing` instead when corpus mutation and code-coverage feedback
35	are needed to explore a parser, protocol, query grammar, file format, HTTP request
36	surface, or other high-dimensional byte-oriented input. Both may be used on one
37	component when they verify distinct contracts.
38	
39	Before writing the property, state:
40	
41	1. the exact system boundary;
42	2. the input domain and invalid subdomains;
43	3. the invariant or reference model;
44	4. documented normalization or nondeterminism that affects comparison;
45	5. state reset and side-effect isolation; and
46	6. the cost per evaluation and resulting iteration budget.
47	
48	Do not derive the oracle from the same implementation path being tested. A
49	round-trip whose encoder and decoder share the same faulty normalization may need
50	an independent semantic check as well.
51	
52	## Install a Compatible Eris Release
53	
54	Inspect Eris release metadata at application time. Select the newest stable release
55	compatible with the PHP runtime and PHPUnit generation that executes PBT. Current
56	Eris release lines have different PHP/PHPUnit support; do not copy this repository's
57	constraint or assume one release spans a legacy PHPUnit 9 leg and a modern PHPUnit
58	10+ leg.
59	
60	Test the target-derived constraint first:
61	
62	```bash
63	composer require --dev "giorgiosironi/eris:<target-derived-constraint>" --dry-run
64	composer why-not giorgiosironi/eris <newest-compatible-version>
65	```
66	
67	Run the confirmed requirement without `--dry-run`. For a real multi-runtime library,
68	verify every maintained lock. Use a minimal union only when Composer must select a
69	legacy Eris line on an older PHP/PHPUnit leg and a modern line elsewhere. In that
70	case, write property tests against APIs present in both resolved lines, or keep an
71	explicit version-specific PBT runner. Do not drop a supported PHP version or weaken
72	the PHPUnit constraint just to install Eris.
73	
74	## Design Generators for the Domain
75	
76	Start with Eris generators and compose them with maps, tuples, vectors, sets, and
77	dependent generation. Create a named custom generator when a domain type has
78	non-trivial validity rules. Generate valid structures directly instead of
79	generating arbitrary values and discarding most of them with `when()` or
80	`suchThat()`; excessive discards reduce useful evaluations and can violate Eris's
81	minimum evaluation ratio.
82	
83	Keep these values reachable where the contract allows them:
84	
85	- empty, singleton, minimum, maximum, and just-outside-boundary values;
86	- duplicate and reordered collections;
87	- Unicode, invalid encodings, reserved tokens, and escaped values;
88	- nullability and omitted versus explicit default fields; and
89	- sequences that revisit a state or repeat an operation.
90	
91	Preserve shrinking. Mapping a generated primitive into a domain value is useful
92	only when failures can still shrink toward a simpler valid value. Avoid opaque
93	Faker calls, time-dependent data, global randomness, or generators that throw away
94	the relationship between a value and its shrink path.
95	
96	For stateful properties, generate commands allowed by the current model state and
97	compare the model with the system after every command. Reset the system before each
98	generated sequence. Eris may re-evaluate the property during shrinking, so the
99	callback must be deterministic and safe to repeat.
100	
101	## Write an Actionable Property Test
102	
103	Modern Eris integrates through `Eris\TestTrait`. Use the generator API supplied by
104	the installed release. A cross-version shape is:
105	
106	```php
107	use Eris\Generators;
108	use Eris\TestTrait;
109	use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Group;
110	use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
111	
112	/**
113	 * @group pbt
114	 */
115	#[Group('pbt')]
116	final class CodecPropertyTest extends TestCase
117	{
118	    use TestTrait;
119	
120	    public function testDecodeInvertsEncode(): void
121	    {
122	        $this
123	            ->limitTo(500)
124	            ->forAll(Generators::string())
125	            ->then(function (string $value): void {
126	                self::assertSame($value, Codec::decode(Codec::encode($value)));
127	            });
128	    }
129	}
130	```
131	
132	Adapt names, generator, property, and budget to the target. `limitTo()` is useful
133	for source compatibility across Eris lines. On a modern-only project, the
134	installed release's `ErisRepeat` attribute may express the same iteration limit.
135	Do not use an annotation or attribute that the resolved legacy line does not
136	provide.
137	
138	Use `#[Group('pbt')]` with modern PHPUnit. Use `@group pbt` with PHPUnit 9. A suite
139	that genuinely executes the same source under both generations needs both forms,
140	consistent with the project's existing cross-version metadata policy. Add the
141	required `#[CoversClass]`, `#[CoversFunction]`, `#[CoversNothing]`, and legacy
142	coverage tags when the strict PHPUnit configuration requires them.
143	
144	Failure messages must identify the property and any context not already printed by
145	Eris. Do not dump hundreds of generated cases. Eris prints an `ERIS_SEED` command
146	for reproduction and shrinks assertion failures; preserve that output in CI logs.
147	
148	## Set an Explicit Budget
149	
150	Eris defaults to 100 evaluations per `forAll()` call, but the right budget depends
151	on generator breadth and evaluation cost. Set an explicit repeat/limit so runtime
152	does not drift with framework defaults. Pure in-memory properties can normally
153	afford more evaluations than database, filesystem, or process properties. Measure
154	locally and leave CI headroom; also bound shrinking time when the installed Eris
155	release supports it and shrinking can invoke expensive side effects.
156	
157	Do not pin a permanent seed in the normal CI run. A fresh seed explores new values;
158	a failing run prints the seed needed to reproduce it. Pin `ERIS_SEED` only while
159	reproducing or verifying a known failure. If replay is inconsistent, fix leaked
160	state, time, locale, external data, or other nondeterminism rather than keeping a
161	single green seed forever.
162	
163	## Isolate PBT from Ordinary Tests
164	
165	PBT must have its own `pbt` group and Composer command. Exclude that group from
166	every ordinary test entry point, including version-specific PHPUnit scripts and
167	ParaTest. Add or merge scripts in the target project, for example:
168	
169	```json
170	{
171	    "scripts": {
172	        "test": "paratest --processes=auto --exclude-group=pbt",
173	        "test:unit": "phpunit --testsuite unit --exclude-group=pbt",
174	        "test:pbt": "@php -d memory_limit=512M vendor/bin/phpunit --group=pbt"
175	    }
176	}
177	```
178	
179	Preserve existing configuration paths, memory limits, test suites, and
180	version-specific wrappers. The invariant is:
181	
182	- normal commands contain `--exclude-group=pbt` and run zero PBT tests; and
183	- `test:pbt` contains `--group=pbt` and runs at least one PBT test.
184	
185	Do not put a global XML `<exclude><group>pbt</group></exclude>` into a configuration
186	also used by `test:pbt`; combined include/exclude selection can make the dedicated
187	command run zero tests. A separate `tests/Property/` directory or testsuite is
188	useful for ownership, but the group remains required because command and CI
189	isolation must not depend on a directory convention alone.
190	
191	Do not add PBT to `lint`, the normal test matrix step, or the ParaTest aggregate.
192	PBT runs independently so ordinary feedback stays fast and a property failure is a
193	distinct CI signal.
194	
195	## GitHub Actions
196	
197	Read `pbt.yml` from
198	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-pbt/` and apply it as
199	`.github/workflows/pbt.yml`. Replace every `REPLACE_WITH_*` sentinel from the
200	target's PHP support, extensions, lock policy, working directory, default branch,
201	and measured PBT runtime.
202	
203	Run the PBT workflow on pull requests and pushes to the default branch so it is a
204	real quality gate, plus `workflow_dispatch` for seed replay. One selected PHP
205	runtime is normally enough because the job checks domain properties, while the
206	ordinary matrix checks runtime compatibility. Use a PBT matrix only when the
207	property itself covers version-dependent behavior or different dependency graphs
208	implement meaningfully different contracts.
209	
210	Keep the manual seed as an environment variable and validate it before execution.
211	An empty seed must leave Eris free to choose a new one. Pin actions to full commit
212	SHAs, grant only `contents: read`, and give the job a measured timeout. Add service
213	containers only for properties that genuinely require them, with fresh synthetic
214	state for every property evaluation or sequence.
215	
216	## Triage a Failure
217	
218	1. Copy the `ERIS_SEED=...` command printed by Eris and replay only the failing
219	   property with the same PHP, dependency lock, locale, and service versions.
220	2. Confirm the displayed shrunk value still violates the stated contract.
221	3. Decide whether the product, property, generator, normalization rule, or state
222	   reset is wrong.
223	4. Fix the cause. Do not filter the counterexample out or lower the evaluation
224	   count merely to make CI green.
225	5. Add the minimized counterexample as a deterministic example test when it
226	   documents a valuable boundary, while retaining the broader property.
227	6. Rerun with the failing seed and again without a seed to resume exploration.
228	
229	## Verification
230	
231	Run the exact commands the target and CI use:
232	
233	```bash
234	composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
235	composer test:unit
236	composer test:pbt
237	```
238	
239	Also verify:
240	
241	- the normal test command reports zero tests from the `pbt` group;
242	- `composer test:pbt` reports at least one property test and more than a token
243	  assertion count from generated evaluations;
244	- a disposable failing property prints a replayable `ERIS_SEED`, shrinks, and
245	  fails the dedicated command; remove the probe afterward;
246	- replaying that seed reproduces the same counterexample;
247	- the ordinary suite, dedicated PBT suite, and every maintained legacy/modern
248	  PHPUnit configuration remain valid;
249	- `git diff --check` passes and actionlint validates `.github/workflows/pbt.yml`;
250	  and
251	- no installed file retains a `REPLACE_WITH` sentinel.
252	
253	## References
254	
255	- [Eris repository](https://github.com/giorgiosironi/eris) — Current compatibility, `TestTrait`, generators, attributes, and examples.
256	- [Eris reproducibility](https://eris.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reproducibility.html) — `ERIS_SEED` failure replay.
257	- [Eris shrinking](https://eris.readthedocs.io/en/latest/shrinking.html) — Counterexample reduction.
258	- [Eris runtime limits](https://eris.readthedocs.io/en/latest/limits.html) — Iteration, duration, evaluation ratio, and generated-size limits.
259	- [PHPUnit test groups](https://docs.phpunit.de/en/13.0/textui.html#test-selection-options) — `--group` and `--exclude-group` selection.

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-phpbench
3	description: >-
4	  Set up reproducible PHPBench benchmarks in a PHP project, including benchmark
5	  design, shared Composer commands, PHPBench configuration, and optional
6	  pull-request comparisons on one runner.
7	  Use when adding, standardizing, or gating PHP performance benchmarks.
8	---
9	
10	# Set Up PHPBench
11	
12	This skill makes benchmarks useful for both local investigation and pull-request
13	decisions. A benchmark is a performance contract over a stable workload, not a
14	fast test suite or a one-off timing script.
15	
16	The PHPBench setups in `k-kinzal/ztd-query-php` and `k-kinzal/peq` show the two
17	layouts this skill commonly encounters. Treat their subjects and revolution
18	counts as project-specific evidence, not defaults to copy.
19	
20	## Inspect the Target
21	
22	Read before editing:
23	
24	- `composer.json`, every maintained lock, PHP constraints, autoload roots, and
25	  existing benchmark or test scripts;
26	- `phpbench.json`, `phpbench.json.dist`, `bench/`, and `tests/Benchmark/` when
27	  present;
28	- the production path and realistic inputs whose performance matters;
29	- fixtures, random generators, clocks, caches, files, databases, containers, and
30	  network calls that can change the measured workload; and
31	- every GitHub Actions workflow, including runner image, PHP version, extensions,
32	  services, lock policy, action pins, permissions, and timeouts.
33	
34	Preserve an established valid layout when standardizing an existing suite. For a
35	new suite, use the top-level `bench/` layout from this skill. Preserve unrelated
36	changes.
37	
38	Keep existing benchmark CI wiring when the request is to apply toolkit settings.
39	A dedicated comparison workflow is a separate capability, not a prerequisite for
40	PHPBench setup. Do not add benchmark guides to the product README or `docs/` as a
41	side effect.
42	
43	## Define the Performance Contract
44	
45	For every subject, determine:
46	
47	| Decision | Required evidence |
48	|----------|-------------------|
49	| Operation | The exact public operation or algorithm whose cost matters |
50	| Workload | Fixed, representative inputs and their size or complexity |
51	| Boundary | Which construction, parsing, I/O, cache warm-up, and cleanup are inside the measurement |
52	| State | What is rebuilt before each iteration and what is deliberately reused |
53	| Metric | Normally elapsed time; add memory or throughput only when it expresses the contract |
54	| Stability | Enough work per iteration and enough iterations to distinguish signal from noise |
55	| CI role | Local-only, PR comparison, or a required relative/absolute gate |
56	
57	Keep different workload sizes as named parameter sets. Do not replace a realistic
58	workload with a tiny input solely to make CI fast. If the full workload is too
59	slow for pull requests, keep a representative PR group and run the complete group
60	manually or on a deliberate schedule.
61	
62	Microbenchmarks over deterministic in-process code are suitable for the default
63	hosted-runner gate. Filesystem, network, database, process, and container-startup
64	benchmarks include host contention and service variance; make them informational
65	on hosted runners. Require them only on a controlled self-hosted runner with
66	versioned images, pre-pulled dependencies, synthetic fixtures, explicit health
67	checks, and cleanup outside the measured region.
68	
69	## Install PHPBench
70	
71	Inspect PHPBench's current release and PHP compatibility at application time, then
72	select the newest release compatible with every development-dependency runtime
73	that installs the benchmark suite:
74	
75	```bash
76	composer require --dev "phpbench/phpbench:<target-derived-constraint>" --dry-run
77	composer why-not phpbench/phpbench <newest-compatible-version>
78	```
79	
80	Run the confirmed requirement without `--dry-run`. Do not copy a version from this
81	toolkit or another repository, widen the target's PHP constraint, or remove a
82	supported runtime merely to install PHPBench. Preserve an intentional existing
83	constraint and update its lock within that constraint.
84	
85	## Layout and Configuration
86	
87	For a new setup, use:
88	
89	```text
90	bench/
91	|-- <Capability>Bench.php
92	`-- <Capability>/...       benchmark-owned fixtures or support classes, if needed
93	phpbench.json.dist
94	```
95	
96	Add a project-derived PSR-4 development mapping for benchmark support classes
97	when they need autoloading. `Bench\\` to `bench/` is the default for a new suite;
98	do not overwrite existing `autoload-dev` mappings. Run `composer dump-autoload`
99	after changing them.
100	
101	Read the configuration template from
102	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-phpbench/phpbench.json.dist`
103	and install it at the project or package root. If configuration already exists,
104	merge deliberately. Keep the local schema path so editor validation follows the
105	installed PHPBench version. Add `phpbench.json` and `build/phpbench/` to
106	`.gitignore`; the committed `.dist` file remains the shared configuration.
107	Keep `storage.xml_storage_path` at `build/phpbench/storage` when using the shipped
108	workflow, or update every corresponding transfer and Artifact path together.
109	
110	The template intentionally sets stable full-run defaults but no global
111	revolutions. Choose revolutions per subject because a parser call and a container
112	startup cannot share a useful value. Adjust memory limits and PHP settings only
113	from the target workload; keep the same settings for the merge target and
114	candidate.
115	
116	Add these Composer scripts, merging with existing scripts:
117	
118	```json
119	{
120	    "scripts": {
121	        "bench": "phpbench run --report=aggregate",
122	        "bench:quick": "phpbench run --report=aggregate --warmup=1 --iterations=3 --retry-threshold=10"
123	    }
124	}
125	```
126	
127	`composer bench` is the review-quality local run. `composer bench:quick` is fast
128	feedback while authoring a subject. Keep both outside `test`, `test:unit`,
129	`lint`, and ParaTest scripts.
130	
131	## Write Benchmark Subjects
132	
133	Use PHP 8 attributes rather than legacy annotations for new subjects:
134	
135	```php
136	<?php
137	
138	declare(strict_types=1);
139	
140	namespace Bench;
141	
142	use PhpBench\Attributes as Bench;
143	
144	final class ParserBench
145	{
146	    private Parser $parser;
147	
148	    private string $input = 'REPLACE_WITH_REPRESENTATIVE_INPUT';
149	
150	    public function setUp(): void
151	    {
152	        $this->parser = new Parser();
153	    }
154	
155	    #[Bench\BeforeMethods('setUp')]
156	    #[Bench\Revs(100)]
157	    public function benchParse(): void
158	    {
159	        $this->parser->parse($this->input);
160	    }
161	}
162	```
163	
164	Replace every example symbol and value. Then apply these rules:
165	
166	- Put construction and fixture preparation outside the measured method unless
167	  their cost is the contract. Hooks are not PHPUnit hooks; declare them with the
168	  PHPBench attributes the installed version supports.
169	- Use fixed representative data and fixed seeds. Never call unseeded Faker,
170	  depend on wall-clock time, or discover a changing source tree inside the
171	  measured operation.
172	- Isolate setup per subject or dialect. A shared hook must not reseed global random
173	  state after another subject's provider has been initialized; seed the relevant
174	  generator after bootstrap and select explicit resource/database versions.
175	- Reset mutable state before each iteration. Do not let one revolution make later
176	  revolutions cheaper unless warmed state is the contract being named.
177	- Make the result observable when the optimizer or underlying extension could
178	  otherwise eliminate work. Do not add logging or broad correctness assertions
179	  to the timed body.
180	- Use `ParamProviders` for meaningful workload classes. Keep provider keys stable
181	  because PHPBench uses the subject and parameter set to pair baseline variants.
182	- Give cheap subjects enough revolutions for a useful timing interval. Use one
183	  revolution for expensive end-to-end operations. Increase iterations or improve
184	  isolation when relative standard deviation remains high; do not enlarge the
185	  regression tolerance merely to make an unstable benchmark pass.
186	- Verify correctness with deterministic tests. PHPBench should measure a known-
187	  correct path, not become the only test of that path.
188	
189	Add an absolute `Bench\Assert` only for an actual performance budget such as an
190	SLA. The shared CI comparison supplies a relative assertion, so do not duplicate
191	that threshold on every subject.
192	
193	## Pull-Request Comparison and Gate
194	
195	When a PR comparison or regression gate is requested, read `bench.yml` from
196	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-phpbench/` and install it as
197	the separate `.github/workflows/bench.yml`. For configuration-only adoption, keep
198	the existing benchmark job and update it to invoke the shared Composer command.
199	Label a standalone run as benchmark execution; a regression comparison requires
200	both revisions. Keep measurements out of the normal test and lint matrix.
201	
202	Replace every `REPLACE_WITH_*` sentinel from target-project evidence. Select one
203	production-representative supported PHP version rather than a version matrix.
204	Match the target's Composer lock mode, extensions, working directory, and
205	benchmark path. Keep the fixed 10% relative-mode threshold unless the project has
206	a documented performance budget that justifies a stricter threshold. Choose
207	`PERFORMANCE_GATE=true` only for stable in-process benchmarks; otherwise retain
208	the comparison and Artifact in report-only mode.
209	
210	The workflow deliberately remeasures both revisions in one job:
211	
212	1. Check out `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`, the current merge-target tip.
213	2. Check out `github.sha`, GitHub's synthetic merge commit for the candidate.
214	3. Install each revision independently under the same PHP and runner.
215	4. Store the merge-target run as PHPBench tag `baseline`.
216	5. Copy that XML storage to the candidate and run with `--ref=baseline`.
217	6. Show PHPBench's aggregate diff in the job summary and upload raw XML, the full
218	   console report, storage, revisions, and tool versions as one Artifact.
219	
220	Do not download the "latest main" Artifact as the numerical baseline. Artifacts
221	come from different machines and times, expire, and are awkward to identify after
222	reruns. They are valuable evidence for review and diagnosis; the same-run
223	remeasurement is the comparison input.
224	
225	The relative gate uses:
226	
227	```text
228	mode(variant.time.avg) <= mode(baseline.time.avg) +/- 10%
229	```
230	
231	PHPBench applies it to each comparable variant and exits non-zero on regression.
232	The aggregate report still appears in the job summary, and the evidence upload
233	runs even when the assertion fails. A positive slowdown requires investigation;
234	a high `rstdev` means the benchmark needs stabilization before it can support a
235	merge decision.
236	
237	Benchmark sources, benchmark-owned fixtures, and `phpbench.json.dist` must be
238	identical on both sides of a gated comparison. The template reports an initial
239	setup PR as candidate-only because no merge-target suite exists yet. Later harness
240	or PHPBench-version changes are non-comparable and fail when gate mode is enabled;
241	review them as a calibration change, then re-enable the required gate after that
242	change reaches the target branch. Protect workflow and benchmark changes with the
243	project's normal ownership review because a PR can otherwise weaken its own
244	measurement or threshold.
245	
246	The default workflow uses only `contents: read`, writes the report to
247	`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and works for forked PRs without secrets. Do not switch to
248	`pull_request_target` to run benchmark code or grant pull-request write permission
249	merely to post a comment. If a repository later requires a conversation comment,
250	publish the already-created Artifact from a separate trusted workflow without
251	executing PR code under a write token.
252	
253	## Verification
254	
255	Before completing setup:
256	
257	1. Run `composer validate --strict --no-check-publish` and `composer dump-autoload`.
258	2. Run `composer bench:quick` and `composer bench`; confirm every intended subject
259	   and parameter set appears and no unrelated test is discovered.
260	3. Run the suite repeatedly and inspect `rstdev`. Stabilize noisy subjects before
261	   enabling the gate.
262	4. If a comparison gate is installed, make a disposable subject slower by more than
263	   10%, confirm the baseline assertion exits non-zero, and remove the probe.
264	5. Confirm `build/phpbench/` and `phpbench.json` are ignored while
265	   `phpbench.json.dist` and benchmark sources are tracked.
266	6. Run `git diff --check` and validate the changed workflow with actionlint.
267	   For comparisons, capture both stdout and stderr from `phpbench --version`;
268	   PHPBench can print its version on stderr. Two empty strings do not establish
269	   matching tool versions.
270	7. Search installed files for `REPLACE_WITH`; a remaining sentinel is a failed
271	   setup.
272	
273	## References
274	
275	- [PHPBench quick start](https://phpbench.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quick-start.html) — Configuration, subjects, stability, and reports.
276	- [PHPBench regression testing](https://phpbench.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/regression-testing.html) — Tagged baselines, aggregate diffs, and assertions.
277	- [PHPBench assertions](https://phpbench.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/assertions.html) — Metrics, aggregation functions, and expression syntax.
278	- [PHPBench storage](https://phpbench.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/storage.html) — XML storage, tags, and later reporting.
279	- [GitHub Actions job summaries](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands#adding-a-job-summary) — `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` behavior.
280	- [GitHub Actions artifacts](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/storing-and-sharing-data-from-a-workflow) — Upload, retention, and access.
281	- [GitHub Actions security hardening](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) — Least privilege and full-SHA action pinning.

1	# ZTD Query PHP
2	
3	[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
4	[![PHP Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/PHP-8.1%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.php.net/)
5	
6	This repository is a PHP implementation of Zero Table Dependency (ZTD). It began with an [article](https://zenn.dev/mkmonaka/articles/c2413d99ae67bb) by M Sugiura ([@mkmonaka](https://zenn.dev/mkmonaka)): ZTD is their idea, we were impressed by it and wanted it in PHP, and we are grateful to the author.
7	
8	It is also an experiment with AI agents. ZTD is complex, and this repository tests how AI agents can build something like it correctly.
9	
10	## Packages
11	
12	| Package | Description |
13	|---------|-------------|
14	| [bison-parser](packages/bison-parser/) | Parser for GNU Bison grammar files, producing a lossless syntax tree |
15	| [container](packages/container/) | Shared container definitions for ZTD Query integration and fuzz tests |
16	| [lemon-parser](packages/lemon-parser/) | Parser for Lemon grammar files, producing a lossless syntax tree |
17	| [requirements](packages/requirements/) | Links source text, EARS specifications, and tests for PHP projects |
18	| [sql-catalog](packages/sql-catalog/) | Catalogs the SQL an application issues, by static analysis |
19	| [sql-faker](packages/sql-faker/) | Grammar-based SQL generator with a Faker provider |
20	| [sql-fixture](packages/sql-fixture/) | Faker provider for generating test fixture data from schemas |
21	| [sql-formatter](packages/sql-formatter/) | SQL formatter with layout presets, built on the sql-parser syntax tree |
22	| [sql-parser](packages/sql-parser/) | Lossless LALR(1) SQL parsers built from the official grammars |
23	| [sql-semantics](packages/sql-semantics/) | Typed statement models and schema binding: names, types, nullability, and value provenance |
24	| [sql-semantics-mysql](packages/sql-semantics-mysql/) | MySQL statement models and binding rules for sql-semantics |
25	| [sql-semantics-postgres](packages/sql-semantics-postgres/) | PostgreSQL statement models and binding rules for sql-semantics |
26	| [sql-semantics-sqlite](packages/sql-semantics-sqlite/) | SQLite statement models and binding rules for sql-semantics |
27	| [ztd-query-core](packages/ztd-query-core/) | Core library: session, shadow store, rewrite planning, and platform contracts |
28	| [ztd-query-mysql](packages/ztd-query-mysql/) | MySQL platform: SQL parsing, classification, rewriting, schema reflection |
29	| [ztd-query-mysqli-adapter](packages/ztd-query-mysqli-adapter/) | MySQLi adapter: drop-in `ZtdMysqli` / `ZtdMysqliStatement` |
30	| [ztd-query-pdo-adapter](packages/ztd-query-pdo-adapter/) | PDO adapter: drop-in `ZtdPdo` / `ZtdPdoStatement` |
31	| [ztd-query-postgres](packages/ztd-query-postgres/) | PostgreSQL platform: SQL parsing, classification, rewriting, schema reflection |
32	| [ztd-query-sqlite](packages/ztd-query-sqlite/) | SQLite platform: SQL parsing, classification, rewriting, schema reflection |
33	
34	## Related Projects

27	
28	jobs:
29	  build:
30	    if: github.event.action != 'closed'
31	    name: Generate documentation for all packages
32	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
33	    timeout-minutes: 15
34	    steps:
35	      - name: Check out the repository
36	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
37	        with:
38	          fetch-depth: 0
39	      - name: Set up PHP
40	        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
41	        with:
42	          php-version: '8.3'
43	          extensions: gd, mbstring, pcntl, mysqli, pdo, pdo_mysql, pdo_pgsql, pdo_sqlite
44	          coverage: none
45	      - name: Install the root project's locked dependencies
46	        run: |
47	          composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
48	          composer install --prefer-dist --no-progress
49	          composer check-platform-reqs
50	      - name: Generate documentation
51	        env:
52	          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
53	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
54	        run: |
55	          repository="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY,,}"
56	          # The generated statement models of the sql-semantics database packages are documented on the published site but left out of the comparison: diffing them class by class exceeds the memory limit and says nothing a reviewer needs.
57	          composer docgen -- --diff="$BASE_SHA" --exclude='packages/sql-semantics-*/resources/*' --base-url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}/pr/${PR_NUMBER}"
58	      - name: Upload the documentation site
59	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
60	        with:
61	          name: package-docs

63	          include-hidden-files: true
64	          if-no-files-found: error
65	
66	  preview:
67	    needs: build
68	    name: Generate and publish the pull request preview
69	    if: github.event.action != 'closed' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
70	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
71	    timeout-minutes: 30
72	    permissions:
73	      contents: write
74	      pages: write
75	      pull-requests: write
76	    steps:
77	      - name: Download the complete documentation site
78	        uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0
79	        with:
80	          name: package-docs
81	          path: build/docs
82	
83	      - name: Check out the documentation branch
84	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
85	        with:
86	          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}
87	          path: .docs-branch
88	
89	      - name: Publish the preview
90	        working-directory: .docs-branch
91	        env:
92	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
93	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
94	        run: |
95	          set -euo pipefail
96	
97	          mkdir -p "pr/${PR_NUMBER}"
98	          rsync -a --checksum --delete ../build/docs/ "pr/${PR_NUMBER}/"
99	          touch .nojekyll
100	
101	          git add --all
102	          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
103	            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch already serves this preview."
104	            exit 0
105	          fi
106	
107	          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
108	            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
109	            commit --message "docs: preview pull request #${PR_NUMBER} at ${HEAD_SHA}"
110	          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"
111	
112	      - name: Build GitHub Pages and wait for publication
113	        env:
114	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
115	        run: |
116	          set -euo pipefail
117	
118	          expected_sha="$(git -C .docs-branch rev-parse HEAD)"
119	          gh api --method POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds" > /dev/null
120	          for attempt in {1..60}; do
121	            build="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds/latest")"
122	            if [ "$(jq -r .commit <<< "$build")" = "$expected_sha" ]; then
123	              case "$(jq -r .status <<< "$build")" in

125	                # Pages can replace a cancelled build for this same commit.
126	                errored) jq .error <<< "$build" >&2 ;;
127	              esac
128	            fi
129	            sleep 10
130	          done
131	          echo 'Timed out waiting for GitHub Pages publication.' >&2
132	          exit 1
133	
134	      - name: Comment the preview link on the pull request
135	        env:
136	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
137	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
138	          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
139	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
140	        run: |

143	          repository="$(printf '%s' "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
144	          preview_url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}/pr/${PR_NUMBER}/"

150	
151	          Generated in diff mode against ${BASE_REF}. Use **Off**, **Diff**, or
152	          **Changes** at the top of the page to select the documentation view.
153	
154	          Updated for ${HEAD_SHA}. The preview is removed when this pull request is closed.
155	          EOF
156	          comment_id="$(gh api --paginate "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments" \
157	            --jq '.[] | select(.user.login == "github-actions[bot]" and (.body | startswith("<!-- package-docgen-preview -->"))) | .id' | tail -n 1)"
158	          if [ -n "$comment_id" ]; then
159	            gh api --method PATCH "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/comments/${comment_id}" -F "body=@${comment_file}"
160	          else
161	            gh pr comment "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --body-file "$comment_file"
162	          fi
163	
164	  cleanup:
165	    name: Remove the pull request preview

169	    permissions:

174	      - name: Check out the documentation branch

176	        with:
177	          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}
178

194	            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
195	            commit --message "docs: remove the preview of pull request #${PR_NUMBER}"
196	          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"

2	name: setup-toolkit-readme
3	description: >-
4	  Set up a minimal README.md for a PHP project: badges, a one-paragraph
5	  overview, Requirements, Getting Started, and License. Use when asked to
6	  create, trim, or restructure README.md, add badges for CI workflows, a docs
7	  site, PHP versions, license, Packagist, or DeepWiki, or link the repository's
8	  DeepWiki page.
9	---
10	
11	# Setup README
12	
13	This skill writes the product README the way php-ai-toolkit projects keep it:
14	the least a reader needs to decide whether to install the package and to run it
15	once. Everything else lives in `docs/` or the generated documentation site.
16	
17	Use this skill only when the user explicitly asks to create or change
18	`README.md`. Applying the toolkit, adding a workflow, or publishing
19	documentation is not permission to rewrite the product README; the other setup
20	skills say the same. If `README.md` already exists, treat it as product-owned:
21	keep the facts and prose in it, add or change only what the request names, and
22	ask before removing a section the user did not mention.
23	
24	## Discover Project Facts
25	
26	Read these before writing:
27	
28	- `composer.json`: `name`, `description`, `require.php`, the `require` entries
29	  a user must provide themselves (extensions, external tools, framework peers),
30	  `license`, `homepage`, and `support.docs`.
31	- `LICENSE`: the license named by the badge and the closing section.
32	- `.github/workflows/*.yml`: every workflow that runs on the default branch is
33	  a status badge candidate.
34	- The docs workflow, the `gh-pages` branch, or `support.docs`: whether a
35	  documentation site is published and at which address.
36	- Packagist: whether `composer require` works without a `repositories` entry.
37	  Check `https://packagist.org/packages/<vendor>/<package>` rather than
38	  assuming; a package that is not there needs the VCS repository entry in
39	  Getting Started.
40	- The default branch name, for `?branch=` on workflow badges.
41	- In a monorepo, the package directory: badges link to the repository's
42	  workflows and to the package's own documentation path.
43	
44	## Template
45	
46	Read the template from
47	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-readme/README.md` and
48	replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` from project evidence. Do not copy this
49	repository's badges, versions, or wording.
50	
51	| Placeholder | Value |
52	|-------------|-------|
53	| `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` | The package or repository name. |
54	| `{{BADGES}}` | The badge block from the Badges section, one badge per line. |
55	| `{{OVERVIEW}}` | One paragraph: what the package is, who it is for, and the one thing that distinguishes it. |
56	| `{{PHP_CONSTRAINT}}` | `require.php` written for people, such as `8.1 or higher`. |
57	| `{{ADDITIONAL_REQUIREMENTS}}` | One bullet per extension, external tool, or peer the package cannot install itself; remove the line when there are none. |
58	| `{{INSTALL_COMMAND}}` | The `composer require` line, with `--dev` for development tools and the `repositories` entry first when the package is not on Packagist. |
59	| `{{GETTING_STARTED_EXAMPLE}}` | The shortest complete example that does something useful: a code block for a library, the command and its output for a CLI. |
60	| `{{LICENSE_NAME}}` | The license name, such as `MIT License`. |
61	
62	## Structure
63	
64	The README has a title, a badge block, one paragraph, and three sections:
65	Requirements, Getting Started, and License. The overview is prose, not a
66	feature list.
67	
68	Add a further section only when the reader cannot use the package without it:
69	a table of supported syntaxes or drivers, a CLI's `--help` output, or the shape
70	of a configuration file. Name that section for its content and keep it between
71	Getting Started and License. Do not add Features, Architecture, Contributing,
72	Changelog, Roadmap, or Acknowledgements sections; architecture and tooling
73	belong to `docs/` and the generated site, and the docs badge is the link to
74	them.
75	
76	Prefer leaving information out over compressing it. A reader who needs more
77	follows the docs badge.
78	
79	## Badges
80	
81	Add every badge the project can back with a real target, in this order:
82	
83	1. The documentation site, when DocGen or another generator publishes one:
84	   ```markdown
85	   [![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-<package>-0969da?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/)
86	   ```
87	2. One status badge per workflow that runs on the default branch (CI, docs,
88	   Context7, and so on), pinned to that branch:
89	   ```markdown
90	   [![CI](https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=<default-branch>)](https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
91	   ```
92	3. The Packagist version, only when the package is published there:
93	   ```markdown
94	   [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/<vendor>/<package>)](https://packagist.org/packages/<vendor>/<package>)
95	   ```
96	4. The supported PHP versions, derived from `require.php` and the CI matrix:
97	   ```markdown
98	   [![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/php-8.1%20%7C%208.2%20%7C%208.3-777bb4?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://www.php.net/)
99	   ```
100	5. The license, from `composer.json` and `LICENSE`:
101	   ```markdown
102	   [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)
103	   ```
104	6. DeepWiki, for every public repository, as described below.
105	
106	A badge must point at something that exists: no workflow badge for a workflow
107	the project does not have, no Packagist badge for a VCS-only package, no
108	coverage badge without a coverage service. Add a badge in the same change that
109	adds its target, never ahead of it.
110	
111	## DeepWiki
112	
113	DeepWiki (https://deepwiki.com) generates a browsable wiki and a question
114	interface for a public GitHub repository. Add its badge to every public
115	repository:
116	
117	```markdown
118	[![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/<owner>/<repository>)
119	```
120	
121	The link is the repository, not a package path: DeepWiki indexes repositories,
122	so a package inside a monorepo links to the monorepo's page.
123	
124	Indexing is free for public repositories but does not happen by itself. Open
125	`https://deepwiki.com/<owner>/<repository>`; if the page offers to index the
126	repository instead of showing a wiki, ask the user to submit it there. The badge
127	renders before indexing finishes, but the link shows nothing useful until then,
128	so say so in the delivery. DeepWiki for private repositories is a paid Devin
129	feature; report that instead of adding a badge that leads to a sign-in page.
130	
131	## Verification
132	
133	After editing:
134	
135	```bash
136	git diff --check
137	```
138	
139	Then check that every absolute link and badge in the README resolves:
140	
141	```bash
142	grep -o 'https://[^)"]*' README.md | sort -u | while read -r url; do
143	  if curl --silent --fail --head --location --output /dev/null "$url"; then
144	    echo "ok   $url"
145	  else
146	    echo "FAIL $url"
147	  fi
148	done
149	```
150	
151	Confirm the install command works as written from an empty directory when the
152	package is public, and that the Getting Started example runs against the
153	installed package. Report anything that could not be executed locally.
